jobs.description:
Esko is creating a new Director, Global Channel Sales role to establish one consistent global partner program for its software business. This leader will assess today’s varied regional approaches and build the commercial and operating model that enables partners to sell Esko’s business-application software effectively—including partner strategy, agreements, program tiers, economics, recruitment, enablement, performance standards, and rules of engagement with direct sales.


Location and travel: This role may be based remotely in Europe, the U.S. Eastern or Central time zones, or Eastern Canada, with convenient access to a major airport. The leader will work extensively across Europe, APAC, and Latin America and must be able to travel globally up to 75%, particularly during the first year as the program and partner network are established.


This is a hands-on builder role and Esko’s first position dedicated exclusively to channel. The successful candidate will have personally built or transformed a global software channel program, recruited partners, and converted program design into measurable channel revenue. Initially, the leader will directly assess and develop partner coverage across Europe, APAC, and Latin America; as the model scales, they are expected to build and lead a global team, including channel managers in APAC and Latin America.


What makes this role distinctive: This is not a mature-program maintenance assignment. You will create the global software partner model, recruit the ecosystem, launch it across multiple regions, and establish the operating discipline that turns partner potential into sustainable commercial performance.


What You’ll Do

  • Assess Esko’s existing regional channel approaches, then design and launch one global software partner program with clear partner types, tiers, eligibility criteria, benefits, obligations, and performance standards.
  • Build the commercial framework, including partner agreements, discount and margin structures, incentives, deal registration, and rules of engagement with direct sales.
  • Recruit, onboard, certify, and enable partners across Europe, APAC, and Latin America, prioritizing coverage gaps by geography, customer segment, and product line.
  • Serve initially as Esko’s first dedicated channel leader, then build and lead a global team that is expected to include channel managers in APAC and Latin America.
  • Own global indirect bookings performance and create a reliable view of partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, revenue contribution, partner productivity, and forecast accuracy.
  • Create joint business plans, partner scorecards, pipeline reviews, and quarterly business reviews that translate strategy into measurable action.
  • Develop executive-level relationships with partners of different sizes, support priority opportunities, and hold partners accountable for forecasting, enablement, and results.
  • Partner with Product Management, Marketing, Sales, Finance, Legal, and Commercial Operations to equip partners to sell Esko’s software portfolio, including new and acquired offerings.
  • Define the systems, reporting, governance, and operating cadence required to scale a consistent global program and improve its economics over time.

What We’re Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • Approximately 8–10 years of progressive channel sales experience, including direct ownership of building or materially transforming a global B2B software partner program.
  • Demonstrated success recruiting and developing a meaningful partner ecosystem and growing channel-driven revenue; able to explain the regions covered, number and types of partners, program scale, time to impact, and revenue contribution.
  • Experience in business-application or ERP-adjacent software channel models; software channel experience is essential.
  • Multi-region channel experience, preferably across at least two of Europe, APAC, and Latin America; North American channel experience is not required.
  • Proven people-leadership experience, including leading remote or globally distributed teams, coaching leaders, and driving performance accountability.
  • Hands-on expertise developing partner agreements, program tiers, economics, enablement, deal registration, forecasting, and rules of engagement with direct sales.
  • Bachelor’s degree and professional fluency in English, with the ability to influence executives, partners, and cross-functional stakeholders across cultures and time zones.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Packaging, print, workflow, manufacturing, or adjacent industry experience.
  • An established, relevant partner network or strong country-level knowledge of potential software partners in target regions.
  • Proven experience consolidating and harmonizing disparate partner programs into a single, unified partner program.
  • Additional language capabilities beyond English and an MBA or other advanced degree

Why Join Us

High-impact mandate: Serve as the principal architect of Esko’s global indirect growth model and shape how partners take the company’s portfolio to market.


Global leadership: Lead a multi-regional channel organization, strengthen strategic partnerships, and expand into underserved routes to market.

This role is for a highly credible researcher who understands the challenges facing colleges and universities, from demonstrating the value of education and improving graduate outcomes to aligning programs with changing employer demand and responding to AI's impact on skills and careers.

The Principal Economist will develop influential research, publish original insights using Lightcast data, and serve as a trusted external voice with university presidents, provosts, researchers, policymakers, foundations, and other leaders shaping the future of higher education and work. The ideal candidate combines academic rigor, a strong publication record, deep knowledge of higher education, and an established network across the academic and research community. They should be equally comfortable developing a rigorous research methodology, presenting findings at an academic conference, and discussing the implications with a room of university presidents.

Major Responsibilities:

    External Thought Leadership

  • Develop and execute groundbreaking thought leadership that advances Lightcast’s mission across global audiences, with an emphasis on education, skills, careers, and labor market outcomes.

  • Lead creative, rigorous, and high-impact research and data analysis that supports Lightcast’s strategic goals and priorities.

  • Translate Lightcast data into compelling messages, research publications, and broader communications and marketing campaigns.

  • Serve as an external-facing labor market expert through media interviews, research papers, blog posts, social media, podcasts, and other public channels.

  • Represent Lightcast at conferences, expert groups, advisory committees, and other influential forums.

  • Build a visible personal brand in coordination with the Lightcast brand.

    • Research Agenda Ownership

  • Define and own Lightcast’s education, workforce, and future-of-work research agenda around higher education and education-to-work outcomes.

  • Identify high-impact research questions and emerging trends that inform institutional strategy, workforce policy, and economic development.

  • Establish a multi-year research roadmap focused on labor market change, talent pipelines, workforce development, skills evolution, and the impact of AI on learning and work.

  • Lead cross-functional collaboration with product, data, and go-to-market teams to ensure research supports strategy, market positioning, and stakeholder engagement.

  • Maintain rigorous methodological standards while balancing innovation, timeliness, and relevance.

  • Leverage Lightcast’s labor market and skills data to generate actionable insights that improve alignment between education, workforce systems, employers, and labor market demand.

    • Ecosystem Influence and Partnerships

  • Build and strengthen relationships with universities, government agencies, think tanks, foundations, workforce organizations, and industry associations.

  • Establish Lightcast as a trusted partner within workforce, education, economic development, and policy ecosystems.

  • Develop strategic partnerships and collaborative research initiatives that expand Lightcast’s reach, credibility, and influence.

  • Advise policymakers, institutional leaders, and partner organizations on labor market trends and workforce strategy.

  • Participate in advisory councils, task forces, and expert networks that shape workforce, education, and economic policy.

    • Business Development

  • Create opportunities to engage prospective clients, partners, policymakers, and other stakeholders through thought leadership and executive-level conversations.

  • Support business development through strategic presentations, executive briefings, proposals, and client-facing research.

  • Advise go-to-market teams on complex customer opportunities, strategic relationships, and high-profile engagements.

  • Generate and influence pipeline through research visibility, speaking engagements, executive networking, and ecosystem relationships.

  • Lead or support opportunity strategy, solution framing, and stakeholder engagement for select high-value opportunities.

Education and Experience:

  • Advanced degree in economics, labor economics, public policy, workforce development, education, or a related field preferred.

  • Significant experience leading research related to higher education, education-to-work transitions, graduate outcomes, the economic value of education, skills, career pathways, or the relationship between education and labor market demand.

  • Experience with a university, institutional research organization, university-based research center, academic research institution, or higher-education policy organization strongly preferred.

  • Demonstrated track record of publishing influential research and translating complex data into clear, actionable insights.

  • Strong relationships across government, education, workforce, research, policy, or economic development ecosystems.

  • Experience advising policymakers, institutional leaders, executives, or partner organizations.

  • Proven ability to develop strategic partnerships and collaborative research initiatives across sectors.

  • Experience supporting business development, executive engagement, client strategy, or commercially relevant research preferred.

  • Background in a leading research institution, university, think tank, government agency, workforce organization, economic mobility organization, or labor market data organization strongly preferred.

  • Experience as a current or former fellow, scholar, senior researcher, policy leader, or practitioner focused on workforce development, labor economics, skills, education, or future-of-work issues preferred.

  • Former White House, federal agency, state workforce policy, or similar public-sector leadership experience is highly valued.

  • Strong written, verbal, presentation, executive communication, and stakeholder management skills.

  • Ability to balance methodological rigor, public influence, relationship building, and commercial impact.

  • Ability to travel approximately once per month, with additional travel for major research launches, speaking engagements, and strategic initiatives.

  • Preference for candidates located in or near Washington, DC, due to the role’s policy, government, and ecosystem engagement responsibilities.

Lightcast is a global leader in labor market insights, with headquarters in Moscow, ID (US) and offices in the United Kingdom, Europe, and India. We work with partners across six continents to help drive economic prosperity and mobility by providing the insights needed to build and develop our people, our institutions and companies, and our communities.

Lightcast is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and does not discriminate on the basis of federally protected statuses. Lightcast has always been, and always will be, committed to diversity of thought and unique perspectives. We seek dynamic professionals from all backgrounds to join our teams, and we encourage our employees to bring their authentic, original, and best selves to work.

jobs.description:
Bring more to life

Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference within life sciences, diagnostics and biotechnology?

At Beckman Coulter Diagnostics, one of Danaher’s 15+ operating companies, our work saves lives—and we’re all united by a shared commitment to innovate for tangible impact.

You’ll thrive in a culture of belonging where you and your unique viewpoint matter. And by harnessing Danaher’s system of continuous improvement, you help turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.

As a global leader in clinical diagnostics, Beckman Coulter Diagnostics has challenged convention to elevate the diagnostic laboratory’s role in improving patient health for more than 90 years. Our diagnostic solutions are used in routine and complex clinical testing, and are used in hospitals, reference and research laboratories, and physician offices around the world. Every hour around the world, more than one million tests are run on Beckman Coulter Diagnostics systems, impacting 1.2 billion patients and more than three million clinicians per year. From uncovering the next clinical breakthrough, to rapid and reliable sample analysis, to more rigorous decision making—we are enabling clinicians to deliver the best possible care to their patients with improved efficiency, clinical confidence, adaptive collaboration, and accelerated intelligence.

Learn about the Danaher Business System which makes everything possible.

The opportunity

The Process Leader, Global Manufacturing Capacity is responsible for developing, analyzing, and driving long-range capacity plans across a global portfolio of manufacturing processes and production lines. The role translates product demand and portfolio growth into technically sound capacity requirements across Beckman Coulter’s internal manufacturing network, critical suppliers, and OEM partners.

It is a hands-on analytical and technical role that works directly with Manufacturing, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations, and Supply Chain teams. The successful candidate will be comfortable going to the production floor, understanding how a line actually operates, challenging technical assumptions constructively, and converting engineering realities into fact-based capacity models and investment priorities.

The position reports to the Senior Director of S&OP, is part of the Global Supply Chain organization.

What you will do

  • Build and maintain end-to-end capacity models for complex manufacturing lines with multiple process steps, variable cycle times, shared equipment, labor constraints, yield losses, changeovers, and product-mix dependencies.
  • Partner directly with manufacturing engineers, operations leaders, maintenance, quality, and site teams to understand line design, equipment capability, process flow, standard work, bottlenecks, and practical operating constraints.
  • Lead technical capacity reviews at the line, value-stream, site, supplier, and global-network levels. Ask the right engineering questions, test assumptions, and create a common fact base for decision making.
  • Translate demand forecasts, mix shifts, new product introductions, transfers, and growth scenarios into equipment, labor, floor-space, tooling, and supplier capacity requirements.
  • Perform what-if and sensitivity analyses to evaluate demand changes, process improvements, yield and uptime changes, alternate routings, capital investments, and risk-mitigation options.
  • Identify emerging capacity gaps early and partner with cross-functional teams to define practical mitigation plans, owners, timing, and decision points.
  • Support capital and network decisions with clear capacity evidence, scenario comparisons, assumptions, risks, and recommendations.
  • Develop and deploy standard, repeatable capacity-planning methods, model structures, definitions, and governance across product lines and manufacturing sites globally.
  • Connect technical capacity conclusions to S&OP and long-range planning, communicating complex findings clearly to both engineering specialists and senior leaders.

Essential qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management or similar field with 9+ years of relevant experience; or a Master’s degree with 7+ years; or a Doctoral degree with 4+ years.
  • Demonstrated experience working with industrial engineering methods to complex manufacturing environments, including line balancing, process-flow analysis, bottleneck identification, utilization, cycle-time analysis, throughput, labor and equipment capacity, and production constraints.
  • Demonstrated experience building capacity models for multi-step manufacturing processes.
  • Ability to engage manufacturing and engineering teams in detailed technical discussions, understand how processes and equipment operate, and translate technical inputs into robust capacity assumptions.
  • Experience with S&OP, IBP, long-range capacity planning, manufacturing strategy, or supply-chain planning.
  • Experience with ERP and planning systems such as Oracle, SAP, Kinaxis, or Anaplan.

Preferred qualifications

  • Degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering preferred.
  • Experience in regulated, high-mix, or technically complex manufacturing, such as diagnostics, medical devices, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, electronics, or precision manufacturing.
  • Experience assessing supplier or OEM capacity and integrating external capacity constraints into end-to-end network plans.
  • Experience supporting capital planning, manufacturing transfers, new product introductions, or major process-improvement programs.
  • Working knowledge of Lean manufacturing, Theory of Constraints, simulation, discrete-event modeling, or statistical analysis.
  • Experience collaborating across multiple sites, regions, and technical functions in a global organization.

Travel and compensation

Up to 20% travel.

The annual salary range for this role is $120,000 to $150,000. This is the range we in good faith believe represents the possible compensation for this role at the time of posting.

The role is also eligible for bonus or incentive pay.

We offer a comprehensive package of benefits, including paid time off, medical, dental, and vision insurance, and a 401(k) for eligible employees. Compensation and benefits are subject to applicable plan terms and the company’s discretion, consistent with law.

Join our winning team today. Together, we’ll accelerate the real-life impact of tomorrow’s science and technology. We partner with customers across the globe to help them solve their most complex challenges, architecting solutions that bring the power of science to life.

Claims and Labeling Manager

Reports to: Standards Senior Director

Remote – US, Europe

About Us

Textile Exchange is a global non-profit driving positive impact on climate change across the fashion and textile industry. It guides a growing community of brands, manufacturers, and farmers towards more purposeful production from the very start of the supply chain.

By 2030, its goal is to guide the industry to achieve a 45% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions within fiber and raw material production. Its focus is holistic and interconnected, accelerating the adoption of practices that improve the state of our water, soil health, and biodiversity too.

For real change to happen, everyone needs a clear path to positive impact. That’s why Textile Exchange believes that approachable, step-by-step instruction paired with collective action can change the system to make preferred materials and fibers an accessible default, mobilizing leaders through attainable strategies, proven solutions, and a driven community.

At Textile Exchange, materials matter. To learn more, visit TextileExchange.org.

Working at Textile Exchange 

We work remotely with a team located in 20+ countries. We are a diverse group committed to harnessing the strengths of the global textile industry to accelerate change toward climate and other key environmental goals. Secondary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Demonstrated experience managing and developing staff, including performance management, coaching and professional development.

In the first phase you are a hands-on caller: you'll cold call into every territory, book qualified meetings for our Account Executives, and prove out the scripts, cadences, and targeting that work. As the function proves itself, you'll hire, train, and lead a team of Sales Development Representatives (SDRs), while continuing to make calls yourself.

This is a player-coach role by design. You'll build the function first, then grow into managing it, and you stay close to the phones the whole way.

This is a build role, not a maintain role. You'll shape the target lists, the messaging, the metrics, and the hiring plan as you go, and you'll have real influence over how TOOLBX opens doors in new markets.

What You'll Do

  • Cold call across all territories. Own outbound prospecting into lumber and building materials, hardware, plumbing, and PHCP distributors and the buying groups they belong to, across Canada and the US.
  • Book meetings that turn into pipeline. Run discovery-lite conversations, qualify against our ICP, and hand off well-prepared meetings to the right Account Executive.
  • Build the playbook. Write and test call scripts, voicemail and email cadences, objection handling, and qualification criteria, then document what works so it can be taught.
  • Build the function. Define targets, metrics, and a ramp plan for the SDR team. Help decide when and who to hire, then recruit, onboard, and train your first SDRs.
  • Coach while you play. Once the team is in place, run call reviews, role-plays, and weekly 1:1s, and keep making your own calls to stay credible and sharp.
  • Work hand in hand with Account Executives. Agree on territories, lead handoff standards, and feedback loops so every meeting is worth the AE's time.
  • Partner with marketing. Use trade shows, webinars, and campaigns to warm up outreach, and tell marketing which messages land on the phone.
  • Bring the market back to us. Share what you hear in the field with product, marketing, and leadership so our messaging gets sharper every quarter.
  • Keep a clean house. Log every call and update every record in HubSpot and report on activity, connect rate, meetings booked, and pipeline sourced.

What You'll Bring

  • 3+ years of outbound B2B sales or business development experience (SDR, BDR, inside sales, or similar), with a record of meeting or beating activity and meetings-booked targets.
  • Comfort making high volumes of cold calls every day, and the resilience to keep your energy up after a rough morning.
  • Strong discovery instincts. You ask good questions, listen, and know when a prospect is worth a meeting.
  • Experience building or improving a process, such as scripts, cadences, or targeting, rather than just following one.
  • An interest in leading people. Prior experience mentoring, training, or managing is a plus, but a clear desire to coach and develop others is what matters.
  • Comfort selling to owner-operated, relationship-driven businesses where the decision-maker's name is on the building.
  • Working fluency with a CRM and sales engagement tools (HubSpot, Apollo, or similar), and the discipline to keep clean data.
  • Self-direction. Remote-first, early-stage, and comfortable with ambiguity.

Bonus Points

  • Experience in building materials, hardware, plumbing, PHCP, or wholesale distribution.
  • Experience selling SaaS, ecommerce, payments, or ERP-adjacent software into distribution.
  • Experience hiring, onboarding, or coaching SDRs or BDRs.
  • Familiarity with HubSpot, Apollo, Gong, or similar sales tools.

Compensation and Why TOOLBX

Compensation: Competitive compensation package benefits and equity will be provided.

  • A proven platform entering new markets. You're not selling vapourware. Our platform is battle-tested by top LBM 100 dealers.
  • Real ownership. You'll build the function, the playbook, and the team rather than inherit someone else's.
  • A team that answers. Fast implementations and responsive support mean our customers stay customers.

Our values: Customer obsessed · Measure twice and cut once · Build foundations that last · Solution-driven thinking · Be curious and ask questions

Company Overview

Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. We convert complex information and operational systems into decisive outcomes, giving public institutions and critical enterprises the tools to move faster, see clearer, and act first in an increasingly contested world.

We are not a consulting firm and not a systems integrator. Every Orbis team is built around practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, and every engagement is judged on one thing: whether it produces working capability, not slide decks. Solutions forged from experience; that is how we build, and it is how we hire.

Job Summary

Lead applied research in one or more Orbis AI focus areas — agentic AI, knowledge representation, dynamic ontologies, autonomous analysis, and high-performance analytics — and carry the results into the product. You will frame the problem, survey what already exists, build prototypes that test a real hypothesis, and measure honestly enough to act on the answer. The role exists because our advantage comes from turning advanced research into dependable mission capability.

Travel: Up to 20% for conferences, customer engagement, and team collaboration.

Key Responsibilities

  • Frame research problems drawn from real product and mission gaps, define what a result must show to be worth productizing, and survey existing work before building.
  • Build prototypes that isolate the question being asked, at the fidelity the question actually requires.
  • Run rigorous experiments — baselines, ablations, held-out evaluation, and honest error analysis — with methodology another engineer can reproduce.
  • Build and maintain the datasets and evaluation harnesses your area depends on, including cases that capture known failure modes.
  • Report results clearly, negative results included, and make a defensible recommendation to continue, pivot, or stop.
  • Transition validated results into production alongside product engineers, staying involved through the handoff rather than delivering a notebook.
  • Contribute to the scientific community through publications, open-source releases, and academic collaborations, and advise Orbis on what in the field is worth adopting.
  • Travel up to 20% for conferences, customer engagement, and team collaboration.

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years of applied research or research-engineering experience, or an M.S./Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field with equivalent applied work
  • Strong Python engineering skills, producing research code another engineer can read, run, and build on
  • Demonstrated experience designing and running experiments that produced an actionable conclusion, with methodology you can defend
  • Depth in at least one Orbis AI focus area: agentic AI, knowledge representation, dynamic ontologies, autonomous analysis, or high-performance analytics
  • Working knowledge of modern LLM and retrieval methods and their practical limitations
  • Clear technical writing that makes a result legible to engineers and non-specialist stakeholders alike
  • Willingness to travel up to 20%

Desired Qualifications

  • Publication record, open-source contributions, or academic collaborations in a relevant area
  • Experience carrying a research result all the way into a production system
  • Experience with knowledge graphs, ontology engineering, reasoning systems, or information extraction
  • Experience with agent architectures, planning, or multi-agent coordination
  • Experience with model training, fine-tuning, or evaluation at scale
  • Experience with performance engineering on data-intensive or analytical workloads
  • Familiarity with OSINT, intelligence, or investigative research workflows

Physical Requirements

  • Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
  • Participation in virtual and in-person meetings
  • Ability to attend planned meetings and/or work in classified spaces for extended periods within the specified work regions
  • Travel: Up to 20% for conferences, customer engagement, and team collaboration.

Orbis Benefits

Beyond the opportunity to work alongside practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, joining Orbis means real ownership over outcomes that matter; the chance to build technology that gives the United States Government and its allies a genuine decision advantage, not just another dashboard. From competitive retirement matching to a PTO policy that encourages real time off, we're committed to creating an environment where our team can do their best work and still have a life outside of it.

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. A full list of benefits is shared with candidates following an initial conversation with our HR team, so you'll have a clear picture of the support and resources available to you as part of the Orbis team.

Orbis Locations

Orbis works in whatever arrangement the mission requires. Depending on the role, that might mean five days a week on a customer site, full-time in one of our offices, a hybrid schedule, or fully remote work; our team is spread across 25 states and four countries to match. We make sure every team member has the tools and access needed to do the work, wherever that work happens.

Travel is common across many Orbis roles, particularly those supporting customer missions in the field.

Orbis is headquartered in McLean, VA, with additional office locations in Taipei, Taiwan, and Canberra, Australia.

qualifications, and business need. Orbis does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law.

jobs.description:
Introduction:

Very Good Ventures is a global consultancy that delivers clients elegant solutions using disruptive technologies. At VGV, we believe that building very good technology starts with a culture of excellence, collaboration, humility, and openness – and of course, have a very good time while doing it. We place our company values and culture at the forefront of everything we do.

Rising to prominence as the foremost Flutter experts, VGV is at an exciting stage of growth as we expand our global presence and our range of strategic services. Our mission is to lead the most influential companies through new digital frontiers and improve the relationship between technology and those that create, manage, and experience it. VGV’s client roster spans industries, including Toyota, Google, Dow Jones, JSX, Betterment, and Norwegian Cruise Lines.

People come to work at VGV to solve challenging problems with the newest technology, alongside some of the best talent in the industry, and in a culture that remains steadfastly dedicated to its employees.

Overview

We are seeking a freelancer to support QA needs on a very exciting new project with a major client. As a Mid-Level Quality Engineer, you will be responsible for improving the quality and reliability of our software applications through meticulous functional testing techniques. Your primary focus will be to identify and define testing scenarios, verify application readiness and report defects, test bug fixes, and contribute to improving our products and processes. Specific projects may need automation skills at either UI or API layers.

Type of engagement: Freelancer
Status: Approximately 40 hours/week
Project duration: 6+ months, depending on project
Location: LatAm

Responsibilities & Expectations

  • Functional Testing: Conduct thorough functional testing of our software applications to verify they meet the specified requirements and deliver a flawless user experience.
  • Test Case development and maintenance: Create comprehensive and well-structured test cases based on functional specifications, design and requirements documents. Maintain accurate testing documentation, including test plans, test cases, and test data case management tools (Testmo for instance).
  • Test Execution: Execute test cases to verify the functionality, usability, and reliability of software products. Check application readiness across different platforms and devices. Execute UI or API automated tests and evaluate its results. Inform stakeholders about testing results. Testing experience with cross browser tools like BrowserStack.
  • Define testing plans depending on the application release, environment and features to be included with test data definition.
  • Defect identification, reporting and tracking: Identify and accurately document software defects and issues, including steps to reproduce, and report them in a clear and concise manner. Perform root cause analysis of identified issues. Monitor and manage defects throughout the testing lifecycle.
    Define defects priority and severity accordingly.
  • Regression Testing: Conduct regression testing to ensure that previously identified issues have been resolved and that new changes do not introduce new defects.
  • Ability to operate autonomously in the definition and execution of testing plans along with any found issues identified.
  • Collaboration and team player: Collaborate with developers, product managers, clients, and other cross-functional teams to ensure effective communication and prompt resolution of issues. Document and share best practices and lessons learned with the rest of the team.
  • Continuous Improvement: Contribute to the improvement of testing processes, methodologies, and best practices to enhance overall product quality.
  • Mobile UI Automation and CI/CD Integration: Design, develop, and maintain automated UI tests for mobile applications on iOS and Android, using frameworks such as Maestro, Appium, Patrol, or Flutter integration tests. Integrate automated suites into CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Bitrise, Codemagic, or similar) so they run on every pull request, nightly build, or release candidate, against emulators, simulators, and real device clouds like BrowserStack. Monitor pipeline results, triage failures, reduce flakiness, and turn automation feedback into actionable insights so the team can ship with confidence and speed.
  • AI-Assisted Quality Engineering: Use AI tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot as part of the daily testing workflow to speed up test design, test case generation, automation scripting, and defect analysis. Build, maintain, and share reusable AI skills and agent workflows (for example, skills that verify Jira acceptance criteria, generate Maestro flows from app exploration, or triage incoming bug reports).

Qualifications:

  • At least 3 years of experience as Quality Engineer.
  • Functional Testing Expertise: Strong knowledge and hands-on experience with functional testing techniques, including test case design, test execution, defect reporting, and regression testing.
  • Analytical Thinking: Demonstrated ability to think critically and analyze complex scenarios to design effective test cases.
  • Ability to plan and operate independently.
  • Attention to detail: Meticulous and thorough in verifying application behavior and ensuring the accuracy and completeness of test cases and documentation.
  • Problem-Solving Skills: Proven problem-solving skills to troubleshoot issues, investigate defects, and propose solutions.
  • Team Player: Ability to work collaboratively in a team-oriented environment and willingness to share knowledge and learn from others.
  • Adaptability: Flexibility to quickly adapt to changing project requirements and priorities.
  • Testing Tools: Proven ability with testing tools and software, such as bug tracking systems and test case management tools. Familiarity with UI and API automated testing frameworks.
  • Mobile Automation and CI/CD: Hands-on experience building and maintaining mobile UI automation for iOS and Android, and integrating automated test suites into CI/CD pipelines, including test reporting and failure analysis.
  • AI Tooling: Practical experience using AI assistants and agents in QA work, including creating or customizing skills, prompts, or MCP-based workflows, along with the judgment to validate AI-generated results.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English to effectively communicate with team members, clients and stakeholders.

Company Values

  • Raise the Bar
  • Grow with Grit
  • Build Momentum
  • Collaborate with Candor
  • Enjoy the Ride

jobs.description:
Acquisitions Associate

Location: San Francisco (preferred) or Remote; travel heavy

Reports to: Head of Acquisitions

Compensation: $140,000–$175,000/yr base + performance bonus + equity

About Bungalow

Bungalow is a technology-driven property management platform consolidating a fragmented $100B+ industry. Through our Landmark brand, we acquire traditional property management companies and transform their operations using AI and automation, scaling while improving service quality. Backed by Khosla Ventures and other top-tier investors, we're growing rapidly through organic channels and strategic acquisitions.

The Role

We're hiring an Acquisitions Associate to own the top of our M&A funnel as we scale through acquisitions. This is a deal-origination role — closer to a private equity associate who builds proprietary deal flow than to a sales development function. Your job is to find the owners of property management companies before anyone else is talking to them and build the relationships that turn into deals.

Reporting to our Head of Acquisitions and partnering closely with the deal and operations teams, you'll spend your time split roughly evenly between two modes of work. About half is outbound: calling and emailing owners and founders to build a proprietary pipeline of acquisition targets. The other half is in the field: traveling to meet owners in person, touring their operations, and representing Landmark at industry conferences and events. Most owners aren't ready to sell when you first reach them, so much of the work is staying close over months — sometimes 12 to 24 of them — so that Landmark is their first call when they are.

This is a hands-on role with a clear trajectory: you'll start by owning top-of-funnel origination end-to-end, then take on more of the deal itself, moving qualified targets through LOI and diligence alongside the deal team, as you grow into a complete investor-operator. It's a build role at a company scaling its acquisition pace, and the pipeline you create is the direct input to that growth.

What You'll Do

Deal Sourcing & Origination

  • Own top-of-funnel: build and work a proprietary pipeline of property management companies that fit our acquisition thesis.
  • Run a high volume of outbound calls to owners and founders of PM companies, supported by personalized email and direct outreach.
  • Build and maintain the target universe — map the market, segment by geography, size, and fit, and prioritize where to spend your time.
  • Manage the pipeline with the rigor of a PE deal team, logging every owner, conversation, and touchpoint in the CRM.
  • Hit clear activity and pipeline targets: outbound volume, qualified conversations, opportunities advanced to LOI, and deals moved into diligence.

Relationship-Building & Market Presence

  • Travel regularly to meet owners in person, tour their operations, and turn early conversations into durable relationships.
  • Represent Bungalow and Landmark at industry conferences, trade shows, and regional events, building a network of owners and advisors.
  • Develop long-term relationships with PM owners across the market, recognizing that most deals here are relationship-driven and take time to mature.
  • Cultivate brokers, industry associations, and other referral sources that feed proprietary deal flow.
  • Become a trusted, recognizable presence in the property management community — the person owners think of when they begin weighing their options.

Deal Support & Diligence

  • Partner with the operations and finance teams to move qualified targets from first conversation through LOI and into diligence.
  • Build the initial picture of a target — revenue, doors under management, owner economics — to assess fit and shape an early offer.
  • Own the seller relationship throughout the process; you're the point of trust for the owner from first call to close.
  • Feed market intelligence back into our acquisition thesis: pricing, seller motivations, and competitive dynamics.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • 2–4 years in private equity, corporate development, or transaction advisory.
  • Comfort with high-volume outbound calling and the persistence that sourcing requires — you treat rejection as part of the process, not a reason to slow down.
  • Strong relationship and communication skills, with the maturity to earn the trust of a founder deciding whether to sell the business they built.
  • Genuine willingness to travel and be in market — you want to spend real time in the field and at industry events, not only at a desk.
  • Self-directed and metrics-driven; you set your own pace and hold yourself to a number with minimal oversight.
  • Comfort operating early — this is a role you help build, not a seat in a machine that already runs.

Strongly Preferred / Not Required

  • Direct sourcing or origination experience — buy-side M&A advisory, SMB deal sourcing, a search fund, or an independent sponsor. If you've done this at a phone-heavy shop and are ready for more time in the field, we'd especially like to talk.
  • Interest in real estate, property management, or SMB roll-ups — you can quickly get up to speed on how these businesses operate and what makes a good one.
  • Genuine interest in how AI transforms an acquired services business, and a desire to be close to where that value is created.
  • Experience with a modern CRM (Affinity, Salesforce, HubSpot) and a system for staying on top of hundreds of relationships.
  • An openness to building deal flow and equity here rather than pursuing an MBA — this role is a real alternative to business school.

Why Join Us

  • Ownership: You own the single most important input to our growth — the top of the acquisition funnel. Every deal we close starts with a relationship you built.
  • Impact: Every acquisition we complete depends on proprietary deal flow, and that flow comes from you. Your work directly enables our growth trajectory.
  • Growth: This role evolves fast — from origination to owning deals end-to-end to a Corp Dev or Principal seat as we scale acquisitions.
  • Equity: Meaningful equity plus deal-linked upside — your compensation scales with the pipeline you build and the deals we close.

jobs.title: Data Coordinator
jobs.excerpt: About Care AccessCare Access is working to make the future of health better for all.
jobs.description:
About Care Access

Care Access is working to make the future of health better for all. With hundreds of research locations, mobile clinics, and clinicians across the globe, we bring world-class research and health services directly to communities that often face barriers to care. We are dedicated to ensuring that every person has the opportunity to understand their health, access the care they need, and contribute to the medical breakthroughs of tomorrow.

With programs like Future of Medicine, which makes advanced health screenings and research opportunities accessible to communities worldwide, and Difference Makers, which supports local leaders to expand their community health and wellbeing efforts, we put people at the heart of medical progress. Through partnerships, technology, and perseverance, we are reimagining how clinical research and health services reach the world. Together, we are building a future of health that is better and more accessible for all.

To learn more about Care Access, visit .

How This Role Makes a Difference

Data Coordinators play an important role in clinical research by helping ensure study data is accurate, complete, and available when needed. As part of a centralized data coordination team, this role helps protect data integrity, and support Care Access’ mission to make clinical trials more accessible to participants everywhere.

Through source data quality control, accurate EDC/CRF transcription, visit-to-entry reconciliation, and proactive query follow-up, Data Coordinators help keep study records reliable and inspection-ready. By catching discrepancies early and helping move issues to resolution, this role contributes to smooth study operations across the Care Access site network.

How You'll Make An Impact

  • Site-Level Quality Control:
    • Review source data collected during clinic visits and work with clinical staff to clarify or resolve discrepancies before information is entered into Sponsor EDC/CRF systems. Responsibilities include:
      • Reviewing source records for completeness, internal consistency, and required good documentation practices.
      • Identifying missing data, incomplete fields, missing signatures, or other potential documentation issues.
      • Reviewing source records for consistency with protocol requirements and study workflows.
      • Documenting quality control activities in the approved Care Access system and tracking items through to resolution.
  • Data Reconciliation:
    • Reconcile study data against supporting documentation to make sure required source records are available, complete, and aligned with study expectations. Responsibilities include:
      • Confirming availability of required source materials, including lab reports, ECGs, imaging reports, and other visit-related records.
      • Reconciling visit documentation against required study data points and expected source records.
      • Maintaining and reconciling adverse event information, informed consent logs, protocol deviation logs, and other study tracking tools.
      • Identifying missing or inconsistent documentation and tracking items through to completion or resolution.
  • EDC/CRF Data Entry:
    • Enter study data into Sponsor EDC/CRF systems accurately and on time, using source documentation and study guidance to support reliable trial records. Responsibilities include:
      • Entering clinical research data in accordance with study requirements, Sponsor expectations, and applicable completion guidelines.
      • Completing data entry within required study timelines and operational expectations.
      • Verifying entered data against applicable source documentation before submission or completion.
      • Applying study-specific EDC/CRF instructions consistently across assigned studies and visits.
  • Query Management:
    • Manage EDC queries and monitor follow-up items by reviewing, routing, responding, and escalating items as needed to keep data issues moving toward closure. Responsibilities include:
      • Reviewing EDC queries generated by Sponsors, CROs, monitors, and EDC systems.
      • Resolving queries directly when responses are supported by existing source documentation.
      • Routing queries that require source clarification, clinical interpretation, investigator assessment, or input from additional site team members.
      • Entering approved query responses into the EDC and monitoring open or ageing queries through resolution.
      • Following up with site personnel when additional input is required and escalating unresolved queries in a timely manner.
      • Reviewing monitor follow-up letter items and coordinating with site staff, where required, to support timely resolution.
      • Reporting monitor follow-up items as quality issues in the Care Access QMS, as applicable.
  • Study and Site Coordination:
    • Work with study teams and site personnel to keep data workflows organized, address open items, and maintain alignment with protocol and Sponsor expectations. Responsibilities include:
      • Maintaining awareness of assigned study protocols, study-specific requirements, and data entry expectations.
      • Prioritizing workload based on participant visits, Sponsor timelines, monitoring visits, and database milestones.
      • Communicating with CRCs, PIs, and site network leadership regarding outstanding data requirements and documentation needs.
      • Participating in study-specific meetings and trainings, as required, to support successful study execution.
  • Other Responsibilities:
    • Support additional data quality, reporting, documentation, and process improvement work as assigned.
    • Maintain study trackers, data logs, dashboards, and other tools used to monitor progress, data completeness, and open action items.
    • Collaborate with cross-functional partners during study start-up, maintenance, monitoring, closeout, and audit or inspection readiness activities, as applicable.

The Expertise Required

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to review clinical research documentation for completeness, consistency, and data quality.
  • Working knowledge of clinical trial data workflows, source documentation, EDC/CRF systems, and query management processes.
  • Ability to interpret and follow study protocols, completion guidelines, standard operating procedures, work instructions, and study-specific requirements.
  • Effective organizational and time management skills, including the ability to prioritize work across multiple studies, visits, deadlines, and competing data needs.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to follow up on open items and work effectively with site teams, study teams, monitors, Sponsors, and cross-functional partners.
  • Ability to spot data discrepancies, documentation gaps, and recurring quality issues, and raise or help resolve them appropriately.
  • Comfort working independently in a remote setting while staying accurate, productive, and responsive.
  • Proficiency with common office and productivity tools, including spreadsheets, shared trackers, email, collaboration platforms, and study related systems.
  • Commitment to confidentiality, appropriate handling of clinical research information, and adherence to applicable quality and compliance expectations.

Certifications/Licenses, Education, and Experience

  • Minimum Education:
    • Minimum high school diploma or GED required; associate degree or bachelor’s degree in life sciences, healthcare, clinical research, data management, or a related field preferred.
  • Minimum Experience:
    • 2+ years experience in clinical research, clinical trial support, healthcare operations, data coordination, data entry, quality control, or a related role preferred.
    • Experience reviewing, entering, reconciling, or maintaining structured data using electronic systems, spreadsheets, trackers, or databases.
    • Experience working with confidential or regulated information and an understanding of the importance of accuracy, documentation quality, and proper information handling.
    • Familiarity with electronic data capture systems, case report forms, clinical source documentation, query resolution preferred.
    • Experience working with internal teams, site staff, monitors, Sponsors, CROs, or other cross-functional partners to resolve documentation, data, or operational follow-up items preferred.
    • GCP, clinical research, healthcare, or data management experience preferred, but not essential.

How We Work Together

  • Location: Remote within the United States. This role requires 100% of work to be performed in a remote office environment.
  • Travel: This is a remote position with less than 10% travel requirements. Occasional planned travel may be required as part of the role.
  • Physical demands associated with this position Include: The ability to use keyboards and other computer equipment.

The expected pay range for this role is $26.00 - $36.00 USD per hour for full time team members.

Benefits & Perks (US Full Time Employees)

We embrace all candidates that will contribute to the diversification and enrichment of ideas and perspectives at AHEAD.

The Senior Enterprise IT Security Architect is a hands-on technical consultant responsible for leading the design and implementation of Isolated Recovery Environments (IREs / cyber clean rooms) for enterprise clients in both on-premises and cloud environments. This role focuses on building truly isolated recovery capabilities that enable organizations to recover critical systems and identity infrastructure after ransomware or other destructive cyber events without risk of recontamination.

You will own end-to-end IRE architecture and deployment leadership, from initial design through implementation and validation, while directing project teams ranging from 3 to 15 people depending on engagement size. The work is deeply technical and client-facing.

Key Responsibilities

    • Lead the architecture, design, and hands-on deployment of Isolated Recovery Environments for on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments.
    • Design and implement strong isolation controls, including network segmentation, air-gapping (physical or logical), one-way replication paths, and firewall/VLAN strategies (e.g., yellow/green models).
    • Architect independent platform services within the IRE (compute, storage, networking, DNS, DHCP, monitoring, and virtualization) with no shared trust or dependencies on production.
    • Design and guide Active Directory forest recovery processes executed inside the isolated environment, including separate identity planes, no trust relationships to production AD, independent time sources, and controlled validation/promotion paths.
    • Define secure administration models, including Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs), restricted access methods (console/iLO preferred; no direct RDP/SSH from untrusted zones), just-in-time access, and integration considerations for PAM solutions.
    • Ensure immutable storage and backup ingestion designs, and incorporate architectural knowledge of platforms such as Rubrik and Cohesity for clean data transfer into the IRE (hands-on experience with these tools is not required).
    • Develop recovery runbooks, validation procedures, and testing approaches so clients can safely restore, scan, and promote workloads.
    • Lead and mentor delivery teams (typically 3–15 consultants/engineers) across design and deployment phases; provide technical direction and quality oversight.
    • Engage directly with client stakeholders to translate cyber resilience requirements into practical, implementable IRE designs.
    • Document architectures, standards, and recommendations for client environments.

Required Qualifications

    • Minimum 10 years of relevant enterprise IT security architecture, infrastructure, or cyber recovery experience.
    • Proven hands-on experience designing and deploying isolated, air-gapped, or highly segmented recovery environments.
    • Strong practical knowledge of network segmentation, firewalling, VLANs, routing controls, and isolation techniques in both on-premises and cloud platforms.
    • Deep understanding of Active Directory, including forest recovery procedures performed in isolation, DNS/time dependencies, and identity separation principles.
    • Experience with platform services (virtualization platforms such as VMware or Hyper-V, cloud infrastructure on AWS/Azure/GCP, storage, and core networking services).
    • Architectural knowledge of modern backup and cyber recovery platforms (e.g., Rubrik, Cohesity) sufficient to design integration and data-flow patterns; hands-on operational experience with these tools is not required.
    • Demonstrated ability to lead technical teams of varying sizes on complex infrastructure and security projects.
    • Strong consulting and client communication skills.
    • U.S. Citizenship required.

Preferred Qualifications

    • Experience with Privileged Access Management (e.g., CyberArk), phishing-resistant MFA, and Privileged Access Workstation design.
    • Hands-on work with immutable storage, object lock, or equivalent write-once protections.
    • Prior involvement in ransomware recovery, clean-room recovery, or large-scale cyber resilience engagements.
    • Relevant certifications (CISSP, CISM, or platform-specific credentials in VMware, Microsoft, or major cloud providers).
    • Experience with Infrastructure-as-Code or automation approaches for repeatable IRE builds.
    • Knowledge of related frameworks or controls (NIST, CIS, or similar) applied to recovery architectures.

jobs.title: Director, Global B2B TPM
jobs.excerpt: Global B2B is Lyft's cross-organizational mandate to build one platform, one product vision, and one integrated plan across every line of business that runs on B2B revenue: US B2B, EU B2B, EU B2G, Chauffeur, AVs, Bikes, and Partner/Protocol integrations.
jobs.description:
Global B2B is Lyft's cross-organizational mandate to build one platform, one product vision, and one integrated plan across every line of business that runs on B2B revenue: US B2B, EU B2B, EU B2G, Chauffeur, AVs, Bikes, and Partner/Protocol integrations. As Lyft has grown internationally through acquisitions like FreeNow, Gett, and TBR, the technology, P&Ls, and org charts have continued to run as separate regional stacks. Global B2B exists to change that: to build a common platform that compounds instead of resetting with every new deal, powering existing US demand while unlocking the lines of business we've had to turn away.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager who can bring order, rigor, and momentum to a program of this scale: one that spans multiple P&Ls, multiple geographies, and multiple functions, all moving toward one plan. You'll report directly to Rishi Dean (VP of Technology and DRI of Global B2B) and will be the connective tissue that turns strategy into a sequenced, tracked, and delivered program. You're technically strong, comfortable operating in ambiguity, and skilled at getting people who don't report to you to move together toward a shared date.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the end-to-end program management of Global B2B: build and maintain the integrated cross-org plan, name every dependency with an owner and a date, and keep the plan honest as priorities shift across Rider, Lyft Europe, Lyft Business, Global Growth, and Finance
  • Run the standing sequencing forum where teams bring business cases, resolve competing priorities, and arbitrate capacity across client commitments, foundational platform work, and expansion opportunities
  • Drive execution across the platform's core layers (e.g., application, sales systems, financial/billing, partner integration, and marketing stack), coordinating single-threaded owners and surfacing where design authority and funding models still need to be settled
  • Track and report program health across every revenue line (US B2B, EU B2B, EU B2G, Chauffeur, Partner/Protocol) and escalate risks to PDT early, before they become date slips
  • Lead the joint planning work between Global B2B and Lyft Europe to align the FreeNow and Gett integration with the Europe roaming and app-launch timeline, converting shared assumptions into written, dated commitments
  • Manage the annual planning cycle for Global B2B, translating scope and business cases into resourced, sequenced initiatives from September through November
  • Build and enforce a consistent product standard across the portfolio, including a scoping gate that keeps requirement changes from silently consuming central capacity
  • Design and run the onboarding path for newly acquired or newly connected businesses (following FreeNow, Gett, and TBR) covering platform, systems, P&L, reporting, and GTM motion
  • Partner with Partnerships, Rider, and MBA to bring AI/agentic surfaces and protocol work into the Global B2B plan from the start, rather than reconciling separate efforts after the fact
  • Communicate program status, risks, and decisions clearly to stakeholders ranging from individual engineers to executive leadership, in a style that is direct, fact-forward, and free of jargon

EXPERIENCE

    • 7+ years of experience in Technical Program Management, Program/Project Management, or a related role, ideally spanning platform, product, and go-to-market work
    • Proven ability to build and hold one integrated plan across multiple orgs with different priorities, scale, and cadences, with a thorough understanding of dependency management
    • Experience standing up or running a sequencing/prioritization forum where competing business cases are arbitrated against shared capacity
    • Comfortable operating autonomously in situations of extreme ambiguity, with only high-level direction, and translating that ambiguity into a written, dated plan
    • Able to communicate highly technical and cross-functional problems and solutions at every level, from individual contributor to C-level executive
    • Experience with platform or infrastructure programs that serve multiple business lines or P&Ls, including shared systems like CRM, billing/invoicing, or partner integration layers
    • Background supporting or working alongside M&A integration (systems, org, or GTM integration) is a strong plus
    • Excellent organizational and planning skills, with the attention to detail to keep a multi-quarter, multi-org program on track
    • Able to influence, negotiate, and inspire others in a matrixed environment where you don't have direct authority over most of the people you depend on

Benefits:

  • Great medical, dental, and vision insurance options with additional programs available when enrolled
  • Mental health benefits
  • Family building benefits
  • Child care and pet benefits
  • 401(k) plan to help save for your future
  • In addition to 12 observed holidays, salaried team members have discretionary paid time off, hourly team members have 15 days paid time off
  • 18 weeks of paid parental leave. Biological, adoptive, and foster parents are all eligible
  • Subsidized commuter benefits
  • Lyft Pink - Lyft team members get an exclusive opportunity to test new benefits of our Ridership Program

Lyft is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace that fosters belonging. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regards to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, age, genetic information, or any other basis prohibited by law. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with applicable federal, state and local law.

This role is fully remote in the US, candidates for this role must be based in the United States #Remote

The expected base pay range for this position is [$217,120] - [$271,400]. In addition to the base pay, this role is eligible for competitive equity awards, bonuses, and benefits. You can read more about Lyft’s employee benefits here.

jobs.excerpt: About Code3Code3 is an integrated marketing agency, powering business growth for digital disruptors and Fortune 500 leaders alike.
jobs.description:
About Code3

Code3 is an integrated marketing agency, powering business growth for digital disruptors and Fortune 500 leaders alike. Our power is at the intersection of Connections, Creative and Commerce – that’s what is in our DNA. By harvesting insights and utilizing audience data, we work with our clients to develop scroll-stopping content and creative that performs and elevates the brands we work with across all digital media platforms.

Our people are energized by challenges and sprint to find unorthodox solutions. We plan, activate and measure as one team, and we’re not afraid to push boundaries and test our way to success. Coders are Relentless, Gritty, Nimble humans who are always striving to be better.

With teams across the U.S., you’ll find more than a job at Code3. You’ll find a place to grow, make an impact, and do your best work alongside a team that’s invested in your success.

The Opportunity

We’re seeking a Head of Paid Search to set the vision for Code3’s paid search practice and lead its next phase of growth. This person will be accountable for the quality and performance of our work, the development of our team, and the growth and profitability of the practice.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can connect paid search strategy to broader business outcomes, while remaining close enough to the work to personally diagnose challenges and guide execution. You will initially lead a team of five, with a mandate to strengthen and grow the team as the client portfolio expands. You will establish Code3’s strategic point of view and operating standards, serve as a senior advisor to clients, lead our Google partnership, represent the practice in the market and be hands-on-keyboard for select large or strategically important accounts.

What you’ll do:

  • Practice Strategy & Innovation

    • Establish the POVs, SOPs and quality standards needed to deliver excellent work across Google and Microsoft.
    • Ensure the practice consistently improves account performance, meets client goals and identifies opportunities for growth.
    • Stay ahead of AI, automation and changing search behavior, translating developments into practical guidance for clients and teams.
    • Connect paid search with Creative, Commerce, Paid Social, Measurement and Client Partnership.
  • Client Strategy & Activation
    • Own paid search performance across Code3’s client portfolio.
    • Serve as a senior client advisor and escalation point, identifying performance concerns, growth opportunities and risks early.
    • Provide strategic oversight and hands-on-keyboard support for select large or complex accounts.
    • Ensure teams deliver strong planning, execution and measurement, translating performance into clear recommendations tied to clients’ business objectives.
    • Partner with Client Partnership on account strategy, executive relationships, retention and expansion.
  • Growth, Partnerships & Market Presence
    • Grow Code3’s paid search portfolio through strong retention, expansion and new business.
    • Lead the paid search strategy for audits, pitches and prospect conversations.
    • Own Code3’s Google partnership and build productive relationships with Microsoft and other key partners.
    • Manage the practice’s staffing, utilization, revenue and profitability in partnership with agency leadership.
    • Build Code3’s market presence through original content, compelling case studies and public speaking.
  • Team Leadership & Development
    • Lead and grow a high-performing team of five, setting clear expectations for strategy, execution, client leadership and accountability.
    • Own hiring, coaching, performance management and career development across the practice.
    • Build the training and operating rhythms needed to improve technical expertise, strategic judgment and client communication.
    • Plan staffing and capacity to balance client needs, profitability, employee growth and sustainable workloads.
    • Foster a culture of curiosity, collaboration, ownership and continuous improvement.

Who will love this role:

  • A builder excited to overhaul and scale a paid search practice, not simply inherit and maintain one.
  • A hands-on leader comfortable moving between executive strategy, team leadership and direct account work.
  • A commercial thinker who connects client performance with retention, growth and profitability.
  • A clear communicator who enjoys developing a point of view, building trust and representing their expertise publicly.
  • A curious practitioner who is actively exploring how AI and changing search behavior are reshaping the discipline.

You should have:

  • 8+ years of paid search experience, including substantial agency experience and deep expertise across Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising.
  • 3+ years leading paid search professionals, including hiring, coaching and performance management.
  • A track record of improving account performance, meeting client goals, retaining and expanding business, and addressing risks early.
  • Experience advising senior clients and leading new-business audits, pitches and strategic presentations.
  • Strong measurement fluency, including conversion tracking, GA4, attribution, incrementality and experimentation.
  • Strong business acumen across practice revenue, profitability, staffing and capacity planning.
  • Experience building effective processes, quality standards and team training.
  • The ability and willingness to work directly in platform on select accounts.
  • Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills.
  • Relevant Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising certifications, or the ability to complete them shortly after joining.

Strongly preferred:

  • Experience with product feeds, Merchant Center and Shopping optimization.
  • Experience across both ecommerce and lead-generation clients.
  • Experience with GEO, AI search or answer engines and their impact on consumer discovery.
  • Established relationships with Google, Microsoft or relevant technology partners.

The position also offers a bonus based on company and client success.

The base salary range will be determined based on the candidate’s experience and geographic location. Certain positions may also be eligible for a bonus, with eligibility and details discussed during the recruitment process. For candidates that are based in California, we encourage you to review this important information for California residents here. For best results, open the link in a new tab.

Salary Range
$134,500—$185,000 USD

Working at Code3

At Code3, we believe great work happens when people feel supported, trusted, and empowered to do their best. We’re proud to offer a competitive rewards package, meaningful opportunities for growth, and a culture that’s collaborative, inclusive, and—most importantly—human.

Here’s what you can expect as a Coder:

A Few Things to Know

Our Interview Process

Role: Marketing Operations Engineer

Description: We’re looking for a highly technical, hands-on Marketing Operations Engineer to own and optimize the systems, tools, and processes that power our marketing engine. This role sits at the intersection of marketing, sales, technology, and analytics. You'll manage our marketing technology stack, ensure systems work seamlessly together, improve campaign execution, and deliver accurate performance reporting. The ideal candidate is a technically savvy problem-solver who thrives on building efficient systems, leveraging AI and automation, and turning complex marketing operations into scalable processes.

What You'll Do

  • Own and manage our marketing technology stack, including Salesforce, Marketing Cloud (Pardot), Qualified, Apollo, aspects of the website, and any other app that touches Marketing.
  • Maintain and optimize integrations between marketing, sales, and revenue operations systems.
  • Build and improve marketing automation workflows, lead routing, segmentation, and nurture campaigns.
  • Manage website updates, landing pages, and forms using AI-powered and no-code tools.
  • Build dashboards and reports to track campaign performance, lead generation, funnel metrics, and marketing ROI.
  • Maintain data accuracy, consistency, and quality across marketing platforms.
  • Identify and resolve technical issues across marketing systems.
  • Partner with marketing, sales, and revops teams to improve lead management and conversion rates.

What We Look For

  • Experience in B2B marketing operations, marketing technology, or a similar technical role.
  • Demonstrates significant experience with MCP, AI-tooling, Github operations, and self-reliance.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Salesforce and marketing automation platforms.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Qualified, Apollo, and similar tools.
  • Understanding of APIs, system integrations, data flows, and automation workflows.
  • Experience managing websites, landing pages, forms, and CMS platforms.
  • Ability to build dashboards, analyze marketing performance, and manage campaign attribution.
  • Ability to work independently and take ownership of technical projects from start to finish.
  • Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate across marketing, sales, and revenue operations.
  • A proactive, resourceful mindset with a willingness to learn new tools and technologies.

What we offer

  • An incredible team of smart and supportive people
  • A deep feeling of satisfaction and completion
  • Fully remote global team working from home
  • Stock options for every employee
  • Flexible work week
  • $400 office stipend
  • Maternity/Paternity leave
  • Student loan debt assistance
  • Pledge 1% - time off during the year for helping nonprofits
  • Health insurance contribution (if in the US)
  • Children's 529 college fund assistance (if in the US)

About Blackthorn

Blackthorn turns any organization's Salesforce® CRM into event planning software powered by their connected data. We're a growing, distributed team with teammates across the globe, and we build Salesforce-native tools that help teams create events, engage attendees, process payments, and measure success — all without leaving their CRM. Our customers range from tiny nonprofits to global corporations, and our products are known for going live in hours, not weeks. We believe the best enterprise software should feel as intuitive as the apps you use every day.

Why our work matters

Most event management tools force teams to juggle disconnected systems, wrestle with flimsy integrations, and spend more time syncing data than planning events. We're building the alternative: a connected platform inside Salesforce that gives organizations richer analytics to prove event ROI, better attendee experiences through personalization and automation, and the flexibility to fit any workflow. Every feature we ship helps our customers spend less time on logistics and more time on the events themselves.

What the job will bring you

A deep level of satisfaction through ownership of your role. You'll get more autonomy than at other companies (our team has told us). Connection. Our team is tightly knit, assisted through occasional team meetups (as we're remote). Challenge. We're trying to move as quickly as possible. This is not for you if you want to sit back and chill. As Ray Dalio says about life, "Meaningful work and meaningful relationships" provide meaning to life. We aim to bring this.

While we are a remote-first culture, we are currently only able to accept applicants in AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, IL, KY, MD, MI, MN, MO, MT, NC, NH, NJ, NY, OH, PA, SC, SD, TX, VA, WA, and WI
