jobs.description:
Full-Stack AI Engineer

Location: Remote (India-based) — Bengaluru preferred; with meaningful daily overlap with our UK and US teams

Engagement Type: Full-time — permanent, ongoing

About MarcoPolo Learning

MarcoPolo Learning is a leading provider of innovative content, technology, and instructional support for early childhood education. Since 2013, we’ve impacted thousands of classrooms and hundreds of thousands of families across North America. Our Emmy-nominated MarcoPolo World School app and The Polos TV series bring STEM and global discovery to life for young learners.

Backed by top-tier investors, we’re on a mission to transform early learning at scale. At the center of that mission is Audrey, our AI Teaching Companion & Coach — a guided AI assistant that helps early-learning educators plan lessons, discover the right materials, and improve classroom outcomes. We’re looking for a Full-Stack AI Engineer to help bring Audrey to life and shape where she goes next.

Role Overview

This is a role for an engineer who loves working where AI meets product. You’ll own the intelligence behind Audrey — the retrieval, generation, and logic that make her genuinely useful to teachers — while being just as comfortable moving across the backend and frontend to bring the whole experience together. You’ll work alongside our backend, infrastructure, and frontend engineers, with real ownership of the AI and real influence over what we build.

Audrey is approaching an exciting launch, and you’ll play a central part in shaping her — refining how she works today and helping define where she goes as we grow into more classrooms.

Just as much as the engineering, we care about instinct for the product. We’re looking for someone genuinely curious about the teachers we serve — an engineer who asks the right questions, understands how educators actually use what we build, and lets that understanding shape the experience. You’ll bring deep AI expertise, a natural instinct for collaboration, and a calm, considered approach to solving hard problems.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the AI at the heart of Audrey — retrieval, generation, and the models and logic that make her intelligent and dependable.
  • Craft an experience where teachers instantly find exactly the right video, printable, or activity, with retrieval that’s fast, accurate, and reliable.
  • Build and refine the content and data pipelines that power Audrey — ingesting and structuring videos, printables, guides, and multilingual content for precise retrieval.
  • Work across the full stack, connecting the AI seamlessly into the wider product alongside our backend and frontend engineers.
  • Shape how Audrey thinks, responds, and guides teachers — designing her behavior, personality, and overall experience with the end user always in mind.
  • Help bring Audrey to launch and shape her evolution as we scale.
  • Continuously raise the quality, speed, and reliability of Audrey’s responses and recommendations.
  • Build fluently with modern AI-assisted development tools to design, build, and iterate quickly.
  • Partner with our infrastructure lead to keep Audrey running smoothly and efficiently in the cloud.
  • Put in place the evaluation, testing, and monitoring that keep quality high, and keep technical documentation clear.
  • Collaborate closely and openly with engineering and product, sharing your thinking and progress early and often.
  • Help shape the product roadmap — from deeper personalization to multilingual support and classroom insights.
  • Build with privacy and safety in mind, including FERPA/COPPA alignment.

What We’re Looking For

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience across the full stack, comfortable working fluidly between backend and frontend.
  • Proven, hands-on depth with modern AI: you’ve personally built and shipped at least one production LLM/AI application. We know the LLM tooling is only a few years old — what you’ve actually built matters far more to us than years on a résumé.
  • Strong experience building retrieval-augmented (RAG) systems — embeddings, vector databases, semantic search, and re-ranking — with a real feel for what makes retrieval accurate and dependable.
  • An AI-native engineer who builds fluently with modern AI-assisted development tools (e.g. Cursor) and weaves AI through their workflow.
  • Strong Python and solid backend fundamentals (APIs, databases, data pipelines), with enough frontend ability to work end-to-end across the stack.
  • Practical LLM orchestration and prompt engineering (LangChain or comparable), including agent/tool design, system-prompt and persona design, and guardrails.
  • Solid AWS experience (compute, storage, databases, containers, monitoring); familiarity with managed model services (e.g. Amazon Bedrock) and/or self-hosted model inference is a plus.
  • A genuine product sensibility — you’re curious about the people who use what you build, and you let that shape your work.
  • A natural collaborator who communicates openly, builds trust across teams, and brings a calm, considered approach to a fast-moving environment.
  • Comfortable owning your work and driving it forward with minimal oversight.
  • Able to work remotely with meaningful overlap across UK and US time zones, with strong written communication.
  • Bonus: edtech or early-childhood education experience; multilingual retrieval; video/audio ML; familiarity with FERPA/COPPA or similar.

What We Offer

  • Competitive, market-aligned salary for an experienced engineer in India.
  • Fully remote, full-time role with flexibility over how you structure your day.
  • End-to-end ownership of the AI behind a flagship product, from launch through scale, with real influence over its architecture and roadmap.
  • A collaborative, family-friendly, mission-driven environment at the intersection of education, media, and technology.

Why Join Us

This is a rare chance to own the AI capabilities of a growing global education company at a defining moment. You’ll be the engineer who brings Audrey to life, shapes how she’s built, and helps take her from launch to a product used in thousands of classrooms. About Thrive

Thrive is a leading full-funnel digital marketing agency supporting growth for some of North America’s most ambitious companies. We evolve our services through disciplined learning, continuous improvement, and close partnership with our clients - regularly assessing what works, what doesn’t, and where to raise the bar.

Our mission is to help companies grow sustainably. To do that, we’ve built deep expertise across performance marketing, brand marketing, digital design, and data and measurement, managing more than $5 billion USD in advertising spend over the past decade. Our work spans startups, scale-ups, and enterprise organizations, including Alo, Zoom, Slack, Uber, Asana, Masterclass, Snapchat, Change.org, and lululemon.

Our culture values curiosity, accountability, and thoughtful problem-solving. We challenge our teams to grow and take ownership of their work while respecting boundaries and long-term sustainability. Thrive is a place where experimentation is encouraged, learning is continuous, and people are supported to do high-quality work they’re proud of - together.

The Opportunity

This is a build-and-grow moment. We're expanding our performance practice around ecommerce, and the work comes with a portfolio most marketers only get to admire from the outside. Think breakout DTC and omnichannel consumer brands, the ones already in your cart, your closet and your feed, whose growth story is still being written. You won't just be running campaigns for them. You'll be the strategic partner helping them figure out how paid media compounds into revenue, customer lifetime value and durable, profitable growth. That means owning the questions that actually move a business: how do we acquire new customers profitably, know which spend is truly incremental, and scale without giving up margin? The tactical craft matters (shopping feeds, creative testing, ROAS, CAC and MER performance), but here it's in service of something bigger: shaping how some of the most exciting consumer brands out there grow. If your idea of success starts and ends with in-platform ROAS, this likely isn't your fit. But if you think about ecommerce as a growth strategy, not just a channel, let's chat.

The Role

Joining the Performance department as Associate Director, Strategy, you’ll deliver strategic leadership to performance teams, leveraging industry trends to evolve Thrive’s services and client marketing strategies. You’ll partner closely with leadership to align team goals with company growth, while managing key relationships and ensuring the long-term success of high-complexity, projects and prospects.

Your focus of responsibilities will be:

  • Domain: Recognized as a leader in performance marketing both within Thrive and in the industry, you make expert contributions to the Performance department, ensuring long-term project success and enhancing the skills of those involved.
  • Client: Championing client success as the hands-on strategic lead across large, multi-faceted accounts, digging into performance, solving problems directly, and refining processes across projects and teams to strengthen client partnerships and retention.
  • People: Manage a team of senior performance marketers and act as an advocate at scale. Helping others elevate their performance marketing skills or add new skills to their toolkit for project growth and performance. ABOUT CHANGING LIVES PRODUCTIONS:

Changing Lives Productions is the in-house video production company of Dhar Mann Studios, the #1 creator of scripted positive content online. BIG PICTURE:

Why This Role Matters: Too much important work still depends on someone remembering to do it. We are seeking an exceptionally resourceful, systems-oriented AI & Automation Operations Manager to design, improve, and manage the processes that support a fast-moving entrepreneur, family office, and administrative team. The objective is straightforward: build systems that make important work difficult to forget, difficult to drop, and easy to execute correctly.

This is not a traditional Administrative Assistant position. We already have team members who can execute tasks. This role steps back, evaluates how work is being done, and asks: Why does someone have to remember to do this? Why isn't there a reliable system for this? Can AI, automation, or better process design make this faster and more dependable? How do we make sure this process is still working six months from now?

The role combines AI implementation, automation, process design, systems management, and high-level administrative operations. It works in close partnership with the Admin Manager and administrative team as a systems and operational partner, strengthening the processes, tools, and infrastructure behind the administrative function rather than duplicating the Admin Manager's role.

HOW YOU'LL SPEND YOUR TIME:

  • Identify repetitive or inefficient administrative work and determine where AI, automation, and better process design can improve speed, reliability, accuracy, and scalability.
  • Build automated workflows across administrative systems and tools so information moves automatically instead of relying on manual updates.
  • Create reminders, triggers, alerts, and escalation systems for overdue or time-sensitive tasks, and automate recurring reports, updates, and status communications.
  • Use AI to research, summarize, organize, draft, and analyze, and develop effective prompts, templates, and reusable AI workflows for the team.
  • Audit how recurring administrative responsibilities are currently handled and find where tasks, information, or follow-ups fall through the cracks.
  • Build and maintain SOPs, checklists, workflows, and operating procedures with clear ownership, deadlines, reminders, escalation paths, and quality control, so important work is verified rather than assumed.
  • Keep recurring processes (inventories, subscription and account reviews, invoice follow-ups, weekly, monthly, and quarterly administrative reviews) running reliably months after they are built, without depending on one person remembering every step.
  • Close loops on open tasks: track follow-ups, escalate when needed, and improve the process so the same bottleneck does not happen twice.
  • Partner with the Admin Manager on priorities, pain points, and process-improvement projects from problem identification through implementation, documentation, and follow-through.
  • Research and prepare concise summaries and recommendations to support administrative decision-making, and organize the trackers, databases, and documentation the team relies on.
  • Evaluate emerging AI tools, train team members on the ones that are genuinely useful, and continuously find administrative work that can be simplified, automated, or eliminated.
  • Step in to support administrative work when necessary, always asking: should this require the same amount of manual effort next time?

WHAT YOU HAVE:

  • You naturally think in systems and processes. You do not just see tasks; you see the system behind them, and you want to simplify, streamline, or automate it.
  • Hands-on experience building real workflows with AI platforms (ChatGPT or similar), AI agents, and automation platforms such as Zapier, Make, or n8n.
  • Working knowledge of Slack, Google Workspace, Airtable, Notion, project-management platforms (Asana, monday.com, ClickUp, or similar), forms, databases, dashboards, and reporting tools. APIs, webhooks, and spreadsheet automation are a plus.
  • Experience turning informal or inconsistent ways of working into SOPs and documented processes that teams actually follow.
  • Exceptional attention to detail, strong organization, and consistent follow-through. You document processes naturally and think through edge cases and failure points.
  • You work independently without constant direction, take initiative instead of waiting for permission, and are comfortable holding people accountable to agreed-upon processes.
  • You communicate clearly and concisely, balance speed with accuracy, and are resourceful when the answer is not immediately obvious.
  • Awareness of AI cost management, security, privacy, and access controls.
  • You do not need to be a software engineer, but when someone describes a repetitive administrative problem, your instinct is to start thinking about how to systemize it.

WHO OVERSEES YOU:

The AI & Automation Operations Manager reports to the Automation Lead. This role works in close partnership with the Admin Manager and administrative team as a systems and operational partner.

WHERE IT ALL GOES DOWN:

This role is fully remote, working from home or a personal office, supporting a distributed administrative team across time zones.

WHEN THE MAGIC HAPPENS:

The typical work schedule is 40 hours a week, Monday - Friday. Specific hours and timezone overlap will be discussed during the interview.

Salary: $12 to $15 /hr

jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Power Digital is an AI-Native Growth Firm built at the intersection of world-class talent and proprietary technology. We help leading and emerging brands grow by combining deep vertical expertise, strategic thinking, and enterprise intelligence to drive measurable business outcomes.

For more than a decade, we have built our business around one belief: the best technology makes great people better. Our teams of strategists, creatives, analysts, and technologists use Omega, our AI operating system, to surface opportunities faster, investigate what is driving performance, and execute approved work with greater speed and precision. Behind Omega is Iris, our proprietary intelligence layer, built on years of real performance data, strategic frameworks, testing, and learnings from across our client portfolio. AI expands the capacity of our people to think, create, solve harder problems, and make better decisions. Human judgment, creativity, and accountability remain central to how we work.

As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. We partner closely with our clients as an extension of their teams, working across strategy, execution, and measurement to identify what is truly blocking growth and determine what to do next. Our culture is built on people who are curious, ambitious, accountable, and committed to delivering meaningful results for our clients and for one another.

At Power Digital, we believe the future belongs to teams that combine the best talent with the best technology. We are building that future today.

**We support 100% remote, in-office, or hybrid work styles for anyone legally eligible to work in the U.S.

A Day in the Life

The Group Director, Consumer Services is Power Digital's senior client relationship and revenue leader for lead-generation-driven businesses across personal finance, home services, hospitality, and other D2C verticals. Your clients live and die by lead volume, lead quality, and speed-to-lead — cost-per-lead, call and booking conversion, and the marketing-to-sales handoff move faster and get scrutinized harder than in almost any other vertical, and you manage your portfolio the way a fund manager runs a book: you know which accounts compound, which lead flow is at risk of drying up or degrading in quality, and exactly where to spend your time. You are the executive a client calls when a sales team starts complaining about lead quality or a call center falls behind on response time, and the leader an Account Director never wants to let down. The roles you consistently play day-to-day are: portfolio growth owner, talent multiplier, tech forward leader and AI systems thinker.

At Power, retention is the floor, not the job. You are commercially driven first: you personally own executive relationships and expansion revenue for the top of your portfolio, and you hold your team to the same standard. In Consumer Services, that means staying closer to lead quality, speed-to-lead, and the marketing-to-sales handoff than almost any other Group Director role requires — because in this vertical, a drop in lead quality or a slow call response shows up in a client's sales pipeline well before it shows up in a quarterly plan. You coach Account Directors and their teams to operate as AI-Native Growth Directors — faster, sharper, and less buried in manual work than the role has ever required before. You decide which AI tools and workflows the division adopts. Your influence runs beyond Client Experience: you shape your Division's go-to-market position, you're a thought partner to your Managing Director and VP, and you represent Power Digital in market on Consumer Services and lead-gen strategy.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own net revenue retention and expansion MRR for the division; treat expansion as the primary commercial lever of the role and own the division's monthly service expansion target
  • Personally own executive relationships across the top 30–40% of the portfolio by MRR — direct relationship, not delegated
  • Run monthly, relationship-focused executive check-ins with top-tier accounts and 1x1 check-ins with every priority account
  • Maintain an accurate, self-owned retention forecast on a weekly basis — accountable for the accuracy of the division's retention data
  • Track vertical-specific marketing signal such as cost-per-lead, lead-to-booked-appointment or lead-to-sale conversion, and speed-to-lead/call response time, since a breakdown in lead quality or responsiveness shows up in a client's sales pipeline before it shows up in a QBR
  • Diagnose risk early and install fixes, not just responses; lead or co-lead quarterly plans for the top 10% of the portfolio, weighted toward strategic outcomes over metrics recaps
  • Partner with Account Directors to build value-based, consultative business cases — expansion should drive value, not be sold
  • Identify and lead common Consumer Services expansion paths, including local and multi-location paid search/local SEO expansion, call tracking and lead-routing optimization, and cross-sell into adjacent lead-gen offers (e.g., financing programs, service plans, membership offers)
  • Keep the Salesforce pipeline current and accurate — stages, forecast, and next steps updated weekly
  • Serve as the frontline for product and vertical innovation, feeding client signal into Power Circuit
  • Build and evolve vertical-relevant reporting frameworks for Consumer Services, including metrics such as cost-per-lead, lead-to-sale conversion rate, and call/booking quality
  • Lead or play a key leadership role in final-round pitches for prospective clients where support is needed (e.g. $25k+)
  • Bring vertical point of view and executive credibility to new business
  • Partner with Sales to sharpen positioning, collateral, and win rate for the division's go-to-market
  • Directly manage Account Directors and oversee the Associate Account Director pod that supports them
  • Coach every direct report to operate as an AI-Native Growth Director, not a task manager — faster diagnosis, more client-facing time, less manual reporting
  • Evaluate the team on Pulse sentiment, health scores, and expansion weekly — not just activity
  • Raise the floor on AI adoption — no one on the team operates the old way
  • Own hiring, staffing, capacity, and career pathing for the division; facilitate DAPs and career progression conversations
  • Practice radical candor; deliver timely, actionable feedback that accelerates careers
  • Identify and develop key talent for future Sr. Account Director & Group Director roles
  • Lead training on vertical-specific and AI-native tools, processes, and strategies
  • Vibe-codes prototypes to automate repeatable tasks, surface better insights, and test hypotheses quickly
  • Designs AI workflows for the team — builds the system, not just uses the tools; models AI-forward behavior
  • Runs Omega and Iris across the full portfolio and acts on the patterns they surface
  • Decides which AI tools and workflows get adopted, when, and how across the division
  • Owns division-level AI quality tradeoffs — where AI accelerates output, and where it must never touch client-facing work unreviewed
  • Builds and evolves Power Circuit solutions specific to the division with AI-assisted research; runs a monthly audit to confirm adoption
  • Collaborates with the innovation team on enhancements and optimizations that better serve the division's clients
  • Consulted on the division P&L and accountable for the profitability of the portfolio
  • Forecast the four pillars — Churn, Service Expansion, New Business, Efficiency — in partnership with the MD and VP
  • Use the P&L and strategic growth bets to build the business case for headcount and investment; drive efficiency through technology, AI, and process improvement
  • Own resolution of every escalation in the direct portfolio
  • Partner with Data Intelligence, Media Planning, and Activation teams to keep strategy and execution connected
  • Represent Power Digital in market — speaking, content, and client-facing points of view
  • Become the internal knowledge hub other leaders turn to for vertical and division expertise

Role Requirements

  • Department leadership and management experience required — has led Account Directors or senior marketers as direct reports
  • 10+ years of leadership experience in a digital marketing agency, with lead-generation client work across personal finance, home services, hospitality, or other D2C verticals at the AD level or above
  • Experience managing a P&L for profitable growth
  • Deep marketing fluency in lead-gen funnels — cost-per-lead, cost-per-acquisition, call tracking, speed-to-lead, and the marketing-to-sales handoff; understands where that connection breaks down (e.g., a lead quality issue that isn't actually a marketing problem) and how to fix it structurally
  • Channel and program strategy expertise — has built or overseen local and multi-location paid search, local SEO, and call-driven marketing programs, not just supervised execution
  • Measurement expertise: attribution methodology for offline conversions such as calls, bookings, and in-store or in-home visits, where common models fall short for multi-location or regulated lead-gen businesses, and how to present alternative methodologies to a skeptical CFO or finance stakeholder
  • Familiarity with regulatory and compliance considerations relevant to lead-gen verticals (e.g., TCPA, state licensing in personal finance) and how they shape campaign and call-handling design
  • Has presented to and pushed back on C-suite and VP stakeholders when the data supported it — can hold a credible, data-backed conversation with a skeptical owner, GM, or finance executive about marketing's contribution to lead volume and quality
  • Expertise in contract negotiation, client retention, and client growth
  • Proven track record delivering high NPS and retention metrics across a portfolio
  • Extensive knowledge of owned, earned, and paid marketing channels — content, SEO and local SEO, paid search, paid social, and programmatic
  • Familiarity with Consumer Services-specific platforms and tools: call tracking and lead-routing platforms, local SEO/listings management tools, CRM systems, and multi-location or franchise marketing platforms
  • Entrepreneurial spirit — energized by building, not just operating; contributes to product and go-to-market strategy, not just client management

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Primary: Meet or exceed a 60% Expansion-to-Churn Ratio (ETCR) on a trailing 3-month average

Secondary Expectations:

  • 105% net revenue retention (trailing 6-month average)
  • 100% MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue) Growth target achievement (set annually)
  • $200K in monthly service expansion pipeline creation across the division
  • +90% employee retention rate
  • Portfolio NPS at or above 8 (trailing 12 months)

Most Important Things (MITs)

  • Division Business & Team Leadership
  • New Business & Service Expansion Leadership
  • Product Quality, AI & Systems Development
  • Client Portfolio Ownership

Power Digital’s people and culture are at the core of our success, which is why diversity in our team’s backgrounds and experiences are paramount. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, and backgrounds, who strive to make an impact inside and outside of the workplace. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employees' points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

Hayward Holdings Inc. (NYSE "HAYW") is the largest manufacturer of residential swimming pool equipment in the world, with a significant presence in the commercial pool market that is continuously growing. Hayward designs, manufactures, and markets a full line of residential and commercial pool and spa equipment including pumps, filters, heating, cleaners, salt chlorinators, automation, lighting, safety, flow control and energy solutions at our company owned facilities. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, Hayward also has facilities in Tennessee, Arizona, and Rhode Island as well as Canada, Spain, France, Australia, and China. 

Hayward Flow Control, a division of Hayward Industries (NYSE "HAYW"), is a leading manufacturer of industrial thermoplastic valves, actuators, filters, strainers, pumps, bulkhead fittings and controllers for use in water & wastewater treatment, chemical processing, aquatics, and many other industrial process applications. Hayward Flow Control is an ISO 9001:2008 Certified manufacturer. 


With a rich history in thermoplastics manufacturing, Hayward Flow Control has been a leader in the industrial flow control sector for over 100 years, renowned for our commitment to quality, innovation, and customer success. We are looking for a passionate and driven individual to join our sales team and contribute to our continued growth.


We are seeking a driven and technically skilled OEM Account Manager to join our team. In this pivotal role, you will be responsible for identifying, developing, and managing key Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) accounts. You'll leverage your deep technical expertise and solution-oriented sales approach to expand our market presence and drive significant revenue growth. If you are a proactive problem-solver with a passion for building lasting customer relationships, we encourage you to apply. This position supports the West Coast.

Account Development and Sales Growth:

  • Strategically identify and target new OEM customers across a range of high-growth sectors, including industrial, water/wastewater, chemical processing, and life sciences.
  • Develop and execute comprehensive sales strategies and business plans to achieve and exceed sales targets and expand Hayward Flow Control’s market share.
  • Manage the entire sales cycle from initial contact to contract negotiation and closing, ensuring a seamless experience for the customer.
  • Proactively seek opportunities for upselling and cross-selling within your existing portfolio to maximize account revenue.

Technical Expertise and Solution Selling:

  • Serve as a primary technical consultant to customers, providing expert guidance on the application and performance of our thermoplastic valves, piping systems, actuation, and related flow control products.
  • Collaborate with customer engineering teams to understand their system requirements, identify specific fluid handling challenges, and recommend tailored solutions.
  • Prepare and deliver technical presentations and product demonstrations that showcase our products' advantages.

Customer Engagement and Collaboration:

  • Build and maintain strong, long-term relationships with key stakeholders across customer organizations, including engineers, purchasing managers, and senior operations teams.
  • Partner closely with internal teams, including engineering, product management, and customer service, to ensure successful product specification, order fulfillment, and a high level of customer satisfaction.
  • Serve as the voice of the customer, effectively communicating market trends and customer feedback to influence product strategy.

Innovation and Market Intelligence:

  • Identify new product development opportunities at key OEM accounts and collaborate with product management teams to influence and drive new product initiatives.
  • Actively monitor competitor activity, industry regulations, and emerging applications to uncover new OEM opportunities and inform our strategic planning.

CRM, Reporting, and Travel:

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all account activity, sales opportunities, and customer interactions using CRM tools.
  • Provide regular, data-driven sales forecasts and performance reports to management.
  • Travel approximately 30–50% of the time to visit key OEM accounts, attend industry trade shows, and support field sales activities.

Requirements:


  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Business, or a related technical field is preferred, with a strong emphasis on materials science or fluid dynamics.
  • Experience: 5+ years of successful technical sales or account management experience, specifically within the flow control, fluid handling, piping systems, or industrial equipment sectors.
  • Technical Knowledge: Strong working knowledge of thermoplastic materials and their applications in various OEM systems.
  • Sales Skills: A proven track record of developing new OEM accounts and achieving sales targets through a consultative, solution-oriented selling approach.
  • Innovation Mindset: A proactive ability to identify gaps in current product offerings and work collaboratively with product teams to advance new product development.
  • Communication: Excellent interpersonal, presentation, and negotiation skills with the ability to engage technical and non-technical stakeholders at all levels.
  • Self-Starter: Highly motivated, results-driven, and able to work independently while consistently collaborating with cross-functional teams to achieve shared goals.

jobs.excerpt: Emergent is a global nonprofit working to mobilize public and private finance to conserve and restore the world’s forests in the fight against climate change and ecosystem loss.
jobs.description:
Emergent is a global nonprofit working to mobilize public and private finance to conserve and restore the world’s forests in the fight against climate change and ecosystem loss. We serve as an intermediary between the private sector and forest nations, acting as a market catalyst to deliver transformational impact for the climate, biodiversity, and Indigenous Peoples and local communities.

Emergent purchases high-integrity carbon credits from ‘jurisdictional’ REDD+ programs – national or subnational forest protection and reforestation programs that are verified to rigorous standards such as ART TREES. We sell these credits to corporate buyers and donor governments looking to drive significant impact and meet their climate and nature goals. We are also working with forest nations to issue and market credits for compliance programs such as CORSIA and various national carbon tax plans. Emergent’s LEAF Coalition is a unique public-private partnership focused on ending and reversing tropical deforestation. By bringing together forest governments, the private sector, donor governments, Indigenous Peoples and local communities, and civil society, LEAF aims to raise and deploy the finance needed to tackle deforestation by making tropical forests worth more standing than cleared.

We have a historic opportunity to bend the climate curve – if we act now. If you are passionate about climate action and the protection of forests, we would love to hear from you.

The Role

Emergent is seeking a dynamic and experienced Business Development / Sales Advisor, Nature Based Solutions (Sales Advisor) to advance new corporate participation in carbon market transactions and expand corporate participation in the LEAF Coalition. The successful candidate will develop the sales pipeline, generate and advance leads, and nurture strategic partnerships that accelerate forest finance and gain influence and access through thought leadership and relationships. The main focus will be driving sales in Europe and Asia, working in collaboration with our Business Development Lead in the US. Our ideal candidate has a strong and evidenced sales background and ideally, a deep network in the corporate climate community and is passionate about driving corporate climate finance towards nature-based solutions.

The Sales Advisor will report to the EVP, Corporate Engagement and drive growth in our distribution to corporate buyers. This is a part-time and flexible consultancy, with the possibility for a full-time staff hire based on business needs and individual performance. Ideally, the Sales Advisor is based near one of our hubs (Barcelona, London, New York), but we are open to qualified candidates based elsewhere. This consultancy will involve periodic travel, depending on leads, needs, and pre-approval from Emergent.

This is a rare opportunity to help shape the future of climate finance while driving real-world results for forests, communities, and the planet.

Responsibilities

  • Lead outreach and engagement with corporate sustainability and procurement teams at Fortune 500 and other companies advancing transactions in the carbon markets. Build strong commercial relationships and generate demand for high-integrity jurisdictional REDD+ credits
  • Lead the development and implementation of Emergent’s comprehensive sales strategy that aligns with Emergent’s goals and market positioning. Maintain a focused and results-based sales pipeline with an effective CRM system. Liaise with US business development lead to ensure progress on the global pipeline
  • Transition clients to and work closely with account managers through deal participation, communications, and credit retirement, with an emphasis on customer growth and satisfaction
  • Track market developments and buyer preferences, and tailor pitches to align with client priorities and Emergent's offerings
  • Address client concerns with clarity, empathy, and a solutions-oriented mindset, emphasizing opportunities for alignment and impact

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in B2B sales, including 3-5 years focused on sustainability, carbon markets, or nature-based and decarbonization strategies
  • Demonstrated ability to close complex, high-value deals in compressed timelines
  • Strong knowledge of carbon markets and nature-based solutions. Familiarity with standards and policies in both voluntary market and compliance markets
  • Entrepreneurial mindset with a track record of building and executing growth strategies
  • Polished, organized, and confident communicator with the ability to translate complex ideas into accessible messages across audiences and formats. Excellent negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Willingness to travel to engage interested buyers as required, and as approved by Emergent
  • Proficiency in CRM systems, digital outreach tools, Excel, and PowerPoint, and able to harness AI to expedite routine processes to keep sales moving
  • Fluency in English required; additional languages (e.g., French, Spanish, Portuguese, German) are an asset

How to Apply

Submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your interest in Emergent and this opportunity.

Our team will review applications on a rolling basis; we strongly encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible. A member of our team will reach out if you are shortlisted for this opening. If your application is unsuccessful, we will be unable to provide individual feedback and will delete your personnel data in accordance with our privacy policies.

Company Overview

Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. We convert complex information and operational systems into decisive outcomes, giving public institutions and critical enterprises the tools to move faster, see clearer, and act first in an increasingly contested world.

We are not a consulting firm and not a systems integrator. Every Orbis team is built around practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, and every engagement is judged on one thing: whether it produces working capability, not slide decks. Solutions forged from experience; that is how we build, and it is how we hire.

Job Summary

Own product surfaces end to end across the Orbis AI portfolio — the Agent Catalog, the OSINT Agent Harness, and Pulse Analytics — from data model through the interface an analyst actually uses. You will build where AI capability meets a real user: streaming agent output, knowledge structures that change underneath you, and results that must be explainable rather than merely plausible. The role exists because mission users judge our products by what they can see, verify, and act on.

Travel: Up to 15% for customer engagement, integration support, and team collaboration.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and ship features end to end — data model, service logic, API surface, and the user-facing interface that consumes them.
  • Build and own the real-time surfaces of the products: streaming agent output, live task status, and progressive rendering of long-running analysis.
  • Make results explainable in the product by surfacing source, provenance, and reasoning path, so a user can judge a conclusion instead of trusting it.
  • Build interfaces over dynamic ontologies and knowledge structures that stay navigable as the underlying representation evolves.
  • Guarantee the service contracts you expose — versioning, backward compatibility, and failure semantics that consuming teams can rely on.
  • Set quality standards for the surfaces you own, including test coverage, accessibility, and front-end performance budgets.
  • Mentor junior engineers and lead design review and planning for the subsystems you own.
  • Travel up to 15% for customer engagement, integration support, and team collaboration.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years of professional full-stack engineering experience with demonstrated ownership of production product surfaces
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, a related technical field, or equivalent professional experience
  • Strong TypeScript/JavaScript across server and browser runtimes, or a strong Python back end paired with real front-end skill
  • Production experience with a modern front-end framework (React preferred), including component architecture, state management, and rendering performance
  • Working knowledge of API design, including versioning, error contracts, authentication, and authorization
  • Hands-on experience with real-time client-server patterns such as WebSockets, server-sent events, or streaming HTTP
  • Willingness to travel up to 15%

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience presenting complex, interrelated data such as entities, relationships, graphs, timelines, or cited documents
  • Familiarity with LLM application patterns, including streaming responses, retrieval, tool calling, and structured output
  • Experience with graph databases or knowledge representation, and querying them at interactive latency
  • Experience building SDKs or developer-facing libraries where other engineers are the customer
  • Experience packaging and deploying to on-premises, disconnected, or edge environments (Docker, Kubernetes, offline installation)
  • Familiarity with accessibility standards (Section 508 / WCAG) in a government or enterprise context
  • Prior experience in a mission, government, or regulated environment where operational reliability is foundational

Physical Requirements

  • Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
  • Participation in virtual and in-person meetings
  • Ability to attend planned meetings and/or work in classified spaces for extended periods within the specified work regions
  • Travel: Up to 15% for customer engagement, integration support, and team collaboration.

Orbis Benefits

Beyond the opportunity to work alongside practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, joining Orbis means real ownership over outcomes that matter; the chance to build technology that gives the United States Government and its allies a genuine decision advantage, not just another dashboard. From competitive retirement matching to a PTO policy that encourages real time off, we're committed to creating an environment where our team can do their best work and still have a life outside of it.

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. A full list of benefits is shared with candidates following an initial conversation with our HR team, so you'll have a clear picture of the support and resources available to you as part of the Orbis team.

Orbis Locations

Orbis works in whatever arrangement the mission requires. Depending on the role, that might mean five days a week on a customer site, full-time in one of our offices, a hybrid schedule, or fully remote work; our team is spread across 25 states and four countries to match. We make sure every team member has the tools and access needed to do the work, wherever that work happens.

Travel is common across many Orbis roles, particularly those supporting customer missions in the field.

Orbis is headquartered in McLean, VA, with additional office locations in Taipei, Taiwan, and Canberra, Australia.

jobs.description:
Why join us?

We’re on a mission to empower people with disabilities to do what they once did or never thought possible. As the world-leader in assistive communication solutions, we empower our customers to express themselves, connect with the world, and live richer lives.

At Tobii Dynavox, you can grow your career within a dynamic, global companythat has a clear, impactful purpose - with the flexibility to also do what truly matters to you outside of work. What’s more, you’ll be part of a work culture where collaboration is the norm and individuality is welcomed.

As a member of our team, you’ll have the power to make it happen. You’ll solve challenges, deliver solutions and develop new, efficient processes that make a direct impact on our customers’ lives.

Candidates must reside within the Eastern or Central Time Zone. This is a remote position that requires occasional travel to our Pittsburgh corporate office as needed.

Work Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM EST


What you'll do:

The Manager, Funded Collections leads the operational performance, people, controls, and continuous improvement of funded insurance collections. The role is accountable for timely and accurate account follow-up, adjustment and write-off governance, denial and appeal resolution, documentation quality, cash acceleration, aging reduction, and compliance across Medicare, Medicaid, commercial payer, and patient receivables. The Manager partners across Funding, Billing, Finance, Accounting, Customer Service, Compliance, Sales, and Technology to resolve barriers throughout the order-to-cash lifecycle. The role is also designed to build the operational breadth, financial understanding, people leadership, and cross-functional partnership needed for potential progression to Senior Manager, based on sustained performance, demonstrated readiness, organizational need, and company promotion practices.

As a Manager, Funded Billing & Collections, you will be responsible for:


1. Funded Collections Leadership

  • Lead daily and monthly Funded Collections operations, establish priorities, balance workloads, and ensure timely execution against cash, aging, denial, appeal, productivity, and quality objectives.
  • Create clear performance expectations, operating routines, escalation pathways, and accountability across collectors and team leads.
  • Monitor portfolio risk and trends, identify barriers to collectability, and implement corrective action plans.
  • Ensure funded insurance balances are worked consistently and supported by complete account documentation and appropriate follow-up.
  • Provide leadership visibility into performance, risk, resource needs, and improvement opportunities.

2. Adjustment and Write-Off Governance

  • Own and maintain a standardized process for preparing, submitting, reviewing, documenting, approving, and entering contractual, small-balance, and bad-debt adjustments.
  • Ensure account reviews validate the patient and chart number, date of service, equipment or HCPCS code, payer, adjustment reason, requested amount, balance location, and supporting documentation.
  • Ensure OMI, AMD notes, EOBs or remits, authorizations, payer correspondence, claim history, and other relevant documentation are reviewed and retained as required.
  • Oversee management review and accurate entry of approved insurance write-offs in AdvancedMD, including the appropriate source, date of service, code, and amount.
  • Maintain approval controls and route requests according to established authority thresholds.
  • Ensure rejected requests are returned with clear feedback and corrected within established turnaround expectations.
  • Identify repeated payer, network-status, timely-filing, billing-method, primary or secondary coverage, and unapplied-cash issues and escalate systemic concern

3. Denial, Appeal, and Receivable Performance

  • Lead strategies to resolve denials, underpayments, authorization issues, timely-filing concerns, coordination-of-benefits issues, and other payer barriers.
  • Ensure appeals and payer follow-up are timely, well documented, supported, and aligned with payer requirements.
  • Use account-level and trend analysis to reduce preventable denials, rework, and write-offs.
  • Partner with Accounting and Finance on collectability, reserves, reconciliations, period-end reporting, and audit support.
  • Create actionable reporting that connects collection activity to cash, aging, risk, and financial impact.

4. Process, Quality, Compliance, and Controls

  • Create, maintain, and govern policies, procedures, work instructions, templates, quality checks, and documentation standards.
  • Ensure requests use the correct adjustment path, one adjustment reason, and one date of service per form when a form is required.
  • Confirm supporting documents are attached, uploaded to the account, and filed in the appropriate shared location as required.
  • Conduct quality reviews and use findings to provide coaching, correct systemic issues, and strengthen first-time-right performance.
  • Ensure compliance with company policies, payer contracts, privacy and security requirements, and applicable laws and regulations.
  • Maintain audit-ready documentation and effective operational controls.

5. Operational Excellence and Technology

  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives that simplify work, reduce manual effort, eliminate unnecessary handoffs, and improve data quality.
  • Partner with Technology and business stakeholders on AdvancedMD, OMI, reporting, workflow, automation, and system enhancements.
  • Use data to identify root causes, prioritize improvements, quantify impact, and confirm sustained results.
  • Build scalable processes and business-continuity coverage that support growth and changing workload demands.
  • Develop business cases and recommendations for workflow, technology, staffing, and capability investments.

6. Cross-Functional and People Leadership

  • Build productive partnerships across Revenue Cycle Operations and other functions to resolve upstream issues affecting billing and collectability.
  • Lead cross-functional reviews, clarify ownership, and create shared accountability for documentation, authorization, enrollment, billing, and payer issues.
  • Recruit, onboard, coach, develop, and retain a high-performing team with clear goals and regular feedback.
  • Develop team leads and emerging leaders through delegation, stretch assignments, succession planning, and role-based learning.
  • Foster a collaborative, accountable, customer-focused culture that supports continuous learning and improvement.

What you'll bring:


Core Performance Outcomes

  • Improved cash realization and predictability.
  • Reduced aged receivables, avoidable denials, rework, and preventable write-offs.
  • Accurate, complete, timely, and consistently approved adjustments and write-offs.
  • Strong documentation quality, compliance, and audit readiness.
  • Clear leadership reporting and timely escalation of material risks.
  • Scalable workflows and technology-enabled improvements.
  • A capable, engaged team with effective team-lead and succession coverage.

Director Development Path

The Manager is expected to expand from strong functional ownership toward broader enterprise leadership. Development should be demonstrated through progressively larger scope, sustained business results, leadership through others, and effective influence beyond Funded Collections.


Director-Readiness Focus Areas

  • Enterprise strategy: Connect Funded Collections priorities to broader revenue cycle, customer, operational, and financial objectives.
  • Financial leadership: Build fluency in cash forecasting, reserves, collectability, write-off exposure, investment decisions, and financial tradeoffs.
  • Organizational leadership: Build an effective leadership structure, strengthen succession coverage, and deliver results through managers and team leads.
  • Cross-functional influence: Lead complex initiatives requiring alignment across multiple functions and senior stakeholders.
  • Executive communication: Present concise, decision-oriented updates that explain performance, risk, options, impact, and recommended action.
  • Technology and scalability: Sponsor material automation, workflow, reporting, or system improvements with measurable business value.
  • Change and risk leadership: Anticipate emerging payer and operational risks, lead mitigation plans, and sustain adoption of new controls and processes.

Example Development Assignments

  • Own or co-lead the annual Funded Collections operating plan and performance review.
  • Lead an enterprise cash-acceleration, denial-prevention, write-off-reduction, or order-to-cash initiative.
  • ·Develop and present a business case for a significant technology, workflow, reporting, or staffing investment.
  • Present portfolio performance, risks, and recommendations to senior leadership.
  • Build a succession and capability plan for the Funded Collections leadership structure.
  • Represent Funded Collections in governance, audit, compliance, or technology workstreams.
  • Process improvement: Lead measurable improvements in workflow, documentation, quality, reporting, and system use.
  • Leadership communication: Provide clear updates on performance, risk, barriers, corrective actions, and support needed.
  • Cross-functional partnership: Lead issue resolution with Funding, Billing, Finance, Accounting, Customer Service, Compliance, Sales, and Technology.
  • Leadership through others: Strengthen team-lead capability, delegate effectively, and build dependable coverage and succession.
  • Financial understanding: Build fluency in cash, aging, collectability, write-off exposure, productivity, and financial impact.
  • Functional ownership: Take accountability for Funded Collections performance, controls, priorities, and follow-through.

Senior Manager-Readiness Focus Areas

The Manager is expected to grow from strong day-to-day team leadership toward broader functional ownership. Development should be demonstrated through sustained operational results, effective coaching and delegation, sound decision-making, and cross-functional partnership.


Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Healthcare Administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • Minimum of four years of progressive healthcare revenue cycle, medical collections, or accounts receivable experience, including at least two years in people leadership or team-lead responsibility.
  • Experience in complex Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, patient receivable, denial, appeal, and reimbursement environments.
  • Experience leading measurable improvement in collections performance, documentation quality, controls, and team capability.
  • Experience with durable medical equipment billing, prior authorization, payer funding requirements, contractual adjustments, and write-offs preferred.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Strong understanding of healthcare collections, payer follow-up, denials, appeals, coordination of benefits, timely filing, contractual adjustments, and bad debt.
  • Ability to interpret operational and financial data, identify trends and root causes, assess risk, and convert findings into action.
  • Experience with healthcare billing, collections, workflow, document-management, and reporting systems; AdvancedMD and OMI experience preferred.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and related collaboration tools.
  • Strong written, verbal, presentation, coaching, and stakeholder-management skills.

Leadership Competencies

  • Strategic and Business Oriented: Connects functional priorities to company objectives and measurable financial and customer outcomes.
  • Ownership and Execution: Establishes a clear path forward, removes barriers, and follows through on commitments.
  • Analytical and Structured: Uses evidence, sound controls, and disciplined routines to improve decisions and results.
  • People Leadership: Develops leaders and teams, delegates effectively, and reinforces accountability and learning.
  • Change Leadership: Builds commitment, manages risk, and sustains improved ways of working.
  • Communication and Influence: Communicates clearly across levels and functions and builds alignment around shared goals.
  • Integrity and Collaboration: Acts ethically, welcomes constructive challenge, and builds trust across the organization.

Work Environment

  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment with interruptions and competing priorities.
  • Ability to collaborate across functions, locations, and levels of the organization.
  • Ability to see, hear, communicate effectively, sit for prolonged periods, and occasionally lift up to 10 pounds.
  • Ability to travel to Corporate office per business requirements.

Career progression is not automatic and depends on sustained performance, demonstrated readiness, organizational need, and company practices.

jobs.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

The Capacity Modeling team ensures Affirm can safely handle forecasted traffic—especially during peak sales events—by translating demand forecasts into concrete, testable capacity plans. They build and maintain statistical capacity models that map traffic inputs (e.g., checkout volume, app opens, batch/job activity) to resource outputs (CPU, memory, connections) and then convert those forecasts into recommended capacity settings such as pod counts, HPA ranges, and/or infrastructure sizing changes across regions and environments.


What You'll Do

· You will be responsible for owning and delivering quarterly goals for your team, leading engineers on your team through ambiguity to solve open-ended problems, and ensuring that everyone is supported throughout delivery.
· You will support your peers and stakeholders in the product development lifecycle by collaborating with product management, design & analytics by participating in ideation, articulating technical constraints, and partnering on decisions that properly consider risks and trade-offs.
· You will proactively identify project, process, technology or business issues, advocate for them, and lead in solving them.
· You will support the operations and availability of your team’s artifacts by creating and monitoring metrics, escalating when needed, and supporting “keep the lights on” & on-call efforts.
· You will foster a culture of quality and ownership on your team by setting or improving code review and design standards for your team, and advocating for them beyond your team through your writing and tech talks.
· You will help develop talent on your team by providing feedback and guidance, and leading by example.


What We Look For

· You have 4+ years of experience designing, developing and launching backend systems at scale using languages like Python or Kotlin.
· You have a track record of developing highly available distributed systems using technologies like AWS, MySQL and Kubernetes.
· You have experience supporting scale up and down of large scale sales event such as Prime Day, Black Friday Cyber Monday, or other sales holidays

· You have tuned autoscaling, CPU/Memory, and multi-threading for compute type workloads.
· You have experience defining a technical plan for the delivery of a significant feature or system component with an elegant, simple and extensible design. You write high quality code that is easily understood and used by others.
· You are proficient at making significant changes in a large code base, and have developed a suite of tools and practices that enable you and your team to do so safely.
· Your experience demonstrates that you take ownership of your growth, proactively seeking feedback from your team, your manager, and your stakeholders.
· You have strong verbal and written communication skills that support effective collaboration with our global engineering team.
· This position requires either equivalent practical experience or a Bachelor’s degree in a related field.

Pay Grade - N

Equity Grade - 6

Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills.

Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents). In addition, the employees may be eligible for equity rewards offered by Affirm Holdings, Inc. (parent company).

CAN base pay range per year: CAD $153,000 - $213,000.

Location - Remote CanadaThis remote role is open only to candidates residing in Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, Ontario, Prince Edward Island, or Saskatchewan.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

#LI Remote

Remote-first with flexibility built inAffirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.

Benefits designed for youOur benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:

  • Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents.
  • Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you.
  • Time off to recharge: Flexible time off and generous holiday calendars help you rest when you need to.
  • Own a piece of what you build: Our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) lets you buy Affirm stock at a discount.

We’re committed to providing an inclusive interview process, including accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you need support, we’re happy to help.

For positions based in San Francisco or Los Angeles: Affirm considers qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, as required by law.

jobs.title: Quality Assurance Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Position SummaryThe Quality Assurance Specialist helps protect the integrity, quality, and reliability of the Maxsold marketplace.
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Quality Assurance Specialist helps protect the integrity, quality, and reliability of the Maxsold marketplace.

This role reviews and executes refund requests, investigates suspicious bidding/selling activity, evaluates higher-risk transactions, identifies catalog quality concerns, and works across departments to address issues that may create customer, financial, operational, or reputational risk.

The Quality Assurance Specialist is expected to assess the available evidence, apply marketplace policies consistently, and make clear, well-supported decisions. This requires strong judgment, attention to detail, curiosity, and the ability to remain objective.

Success in this role is not simply identifying that something may be wrong. It requires determining what can be established, identifying what information is still needed, recommending or executing the appropriate action, and documenting the reasoning clearly.

What You Will Own

Refund Review and Resolution

  • Review refund requests submitted by buyers.
  • Assess buyer claims against listing information, photographs, communications, pickup reports from sellers, marketplace policies, and other available evidence.
  • Identify gaps, inconsistencies, or unsupported claims within the information provided and work to clarify them.
  • Request or coordinate the collection of additional evidence when required.
  • Determine whether refund requests should be approved, denied, or escalated for further review.
  • Execute approved refunds and ensure the appropriate internal or seller-funded treatment is applied.
  • Communicate refund decisions and supporting rationale clearly to the appropriate internal teams.
  • Identify repeated refund patterns involving buyers, sellers, listings, auction practices, or specific items.
  • Maintain accurate and complete records of decisions, evidence, and outcomes.

High-Risk Transaction Review

  • Review flagged first purchases and other transactions identified as presenting elevated risk.
  • Assess available account, payment, bidding, purchase, and behavioural information.
  • Determine whether activity can proceed, requires additional verification, or should be restricted or escalated.
  • Identify patterns that may indicate account misuse, payment risk, fraud, or coordinated activity.
  • Balance risk prevention with the need to avoid unnecessarily disrupting legitimate customers.
  • Document findings and decisions in a clear and reviewable manner.

Suspicious Bidding and Marketplace Conduct

  • Investigate reports or system flags involving suspicious bidding activity.
  • Review account connections, bidding patterns, payment information, refund behaviour, auction participation, and other relevant facts.
  • Distinguish between confirmed facts, risk indicators, and unproven assumptions.
  • Determine whether activity requires monitoring, education, restrictions, suspension, or leadership review.
  • Coordinate with Support, Finance, Sales, Customer Success, or Operations leadership where seller or buyer action may be required.
  • Maintain confidentiality and avoid disclosing sensitive investigation methods or account information unnecessarily.

Catalog and Auction Quality

  • Review auction catalogs before launch for prohibited items and marketplace risk.
  • Work with Seller Support, partners, and other internal teams to correct issues before launch.
  • Apply quality standards consistently while recognizing differences in auction type, category, and risk.
  • Identify repeated quality concerns and recommend education, process changes, or additional review.
  • Help improve catalog standards, review criteria, and preventive quality controls.

Fraud and Chargeback Risk Support

  • Identify transactions, accounts, or operational practices that may create fraud or chargeback exposure.
  • Gather and organize evidence required for internal review or chargeback response.
  • Work with Finance and Support to ensure relevant account, payment, communication, and pickup information is available.
  • Identify recurring causes of chargebacks and recommend preventive actions.
  • Escalate material financial or marketplace risk promptly.

Cross-Departmental Collaboration

  • Work closely with Buyer Support, Seller Support, Finance, Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Operations leadership.
  • Provide clear, evidence-based guidance when other teams flag refund, fraud, bidding, catalog, or marketplace concerns.
  • Ask focused questions that help teams gather the information required for a decision.
  • Explain decisions and policy applications clearly.
  • Escalate complex or high-impact matters with complete context, supporting evidence, and a recommended next step.

Policy and Process Improvement

  • Surface emerging risk patterns and marketplace behaviours.
  • Recommend improvements to refund processes, catalog review, fraud controls, escalation standards, and internal documentation.
  • Participate in audits and targeted reviews of buyers, sellers, partners, auctions, or internal processes.

What You Bring

  • 3+ years experience in quality assurance, fraud prevention, dispute resolution, refunds, risk operations, marketplace operations, investigations, or a related field.
  • Strong critical-thinking and analytical skills.
  • Sound judgment when working with incomplete, conflicting, or emotionally presented information.
  • The ability to assess evidence objectively and separate facts from assumptions.
  • Strong written communication and documentation skills.
  • The confidence to make and explain decisions based on policy and available evidence.
  • A high level of attention to detail.
  • Curiosity and persistence when investigating unfamiliar or complex issues.
  • The ability to recognize patterns across accounts, transactions, auctions, and customer behaviour.
  • Strong organization and case-management habits.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities and time-sensitive reviews.
  • Comfort collaborating with multiple departments and challenging conclusions respectfully.
  • Discretion when handling confidential, sensitive, or potentially fraudulent activity.
  • The ability to remain calm and objective when decisions may be disputed.

Preferred Qualifications

  • A degree in a technical, analytical, or STEM-related field is strongly preferred, including Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Information Systems, Business Analytics, Economics, Operations, or another related discipline.
  • Candidates without a traditional STEM degree may be considered if they can demonstrate strong analytical ability, technical aptitude, structured problem-solving, and experience learning complex systems.
  • 4+ years of experience in customer support, quality assurance, fraud or risk operations, dispute resolution, investigations, marketplace operations, or another role where you were responsible for reviewing information and making customer-impacting decision
  • Experience reviewing refund, fraud, payment, chargeback, or account-risk cases.
  • Familiarity with ticketing, CRM, payment-processing, or case-management systems.
  • Experience interpreting and applying customer-facing policies.
  • Experience reviewing product listings, catalogs, claims, or marketplace content.
  • Experience conducting audits or pattern-based investigations.
  • Familiarity with payment disputes, account verification, or transaction-risk indicators.
  • A track record of identifying process gaps and recommending practical improvements.

What Success Looks Like

A successful Quality Assurance Specialist:

  • Makes timely, consistent, and evidence-based decisions.
  • Applies policy accurately while recognizing when a matter requires additional judgment.
  • Approves valid refund requests and confidently denies unsupported requests.
  • Produces clear documentation that explains what happened, what evidence was reviewed, and why a decision was made.
  • Recognizes suspicious patterns and escalates them at the appropriate level.
  • Balances thoroughness with the need to make timely decisions.
  • Focuses effort on material customer, financial, operational, and reputational risk.
  • Contributes to stronger policies, processes, and preventive controls.
  • Earns trust through consistency, objectivity, discretion, and sound judgment.

Why This Role Matters

Quality Assurance protects the marketplace from preventable loss and harmful activity while ensuring suspicious behaviour, policy enforcement, and quality concerns are reviewed appropriately.

The work performed by this team affects buyer confidence, end-user accountability, auction quality, refund exposure, fraud prevention, chargeback risk, and Maxsold’s broader reputation.

This role is well suited to someone who enjoys investigating complex situations, weighing evidence, making defensible decisions, and improving the systems that protect a marketplace.

Come join a company who is a key leader in the industry scaling the next core commerce infrastructure and on the path from $100M to $500M! Founded in 2012, Salsify helps brand manufacturers, distributors, and retailers in over 80 countries collaborate to win on the digital shelf. As the market leader globally, our products are shopper-centric, frictionless, and create memorable commerce experiences. Our products provide a competitive edge through experiences that improve brand trust, amplify product differentiation and assortments, increase conversion rate, improve profit margins, and speed time to market.

Learn how the world’s largest brands, including Mars, L'Oreal, Coca-Cola, Bosch, and GSK, as well as retailers and distributors such as E.Leclerc, Carrefour, Metro, and Intermarché use Salsify everyday to stand out on the digital shelf.

At Salsify, we strive to embody an equitable, diverse, and inclusive company culture. We are united across countries, levels, tenures, and a host of other dimensions of diversity. We understand that while work is just one aspect of who we are, a truly inclusive culture accounts for the full authenticity of every single human being that works here.

About the Opportunity

Salsify is seeking a highly motivated, dynamic, and driven Enterprise Account Executive (New Logo Hunter) who has previous enterprise SaaS experience and an affinity for solution selling. As an Enterprise Account Executive at Salsify, you will be responsible for prospecting, pitching, and winning net-new enterprise accounts. This includes selling our Salsify PXM Advance platform, associated add-on modules, and professional services to large, multi-national, multi-billion dollar brand manufacturers that are not yet Salsify customers.

Enterprise Account Executives are responsible for taking a strategic, outbound sales approach to break into target accounts and establish Salsify’s presence within the world's most well-known brand manufacturers. We have found that the most successful Hunter Account Executives are relentless prospectors and masterful storytellers who can weave a complex solution into connecting with net-new brands, helping them optimize how they navigate the ever-changing e-commerce landscape. Salsify is seeing incredible success and growth, and our Enterprise Hunters are the primary engine driving our market expansion on the worldwide stage. We are seeking high achievers who thrive on the thrill of the hunt, set the bar for net-new customer acquisition, and act as true evangelists in their sales approach.

How You'll Make an Impact:

  • Drive rigorous, outbound territory planning and prospecting to identify, penetrate, and secure new greenfield enterprise accounts.
  • Initiate and cultivate executive-level relationships (CMO, VP, C-Suite) across prospective multi-billion dollar brand manufacturers to build urgency and quantify business value.
  • Run full-cycle, complex sales processes from initial cold outreach and discovery through contract negotiation and execution.
  • Work cross-functionally with Salsify’s key internal teams—including Sales Engineering, Business Development, Product, and Legal—to build winning deal strategies and custom value propositions.
  • Employ a proven, repeatable sales methodology to build business value, leverage internal champions, and consistently close net-new multi-year contracts.

You'll Enjoy This Role If You Have:

  • Spent the last 6-8+ years consistently exceeding an assigned net-new ARR/quota within the large enterprise segment (500M–2B+ in revenue).
  • A proven track record as a pure hunter, with deep experience in cold prospecting, multi-threading prospective accounts, and winning greenfield SaaS logos.
  • Sold complex SaaS solutions directly to enterprise business units and key personas, including CMOs, Chief Digital Officers, VPs, and Directors.
  • Demonstrated success executing multiple complex, long-cycle enterprise sales processes concurrently in a competitive landscape.
  • Experience mapping and penetrating Fortune 100/500/1000 targets without relying on existing customer relationships or warm handoffs.
  • Professional sales training and strict adherence to a repeatable sales process; mastery of MEDDPICC/MEDDIC is highly preferred.
At Salsify, we maintain 3 core principles as part of our Compensation Philosophy:
  • We pay market rates, which are competitive and equitable
  • We pay based on performance and proficiency, not tenure
  • We adjust proactively; when the market moves, we do too
The posted compensation range reflects the base salary for this position. In addition to base salary, some eligible roles may also have a commission plan or a bonus incentive. All full-time employees are invited to participate in our Total Rewards plan, which includes health & medical benefits, PTO, and more. Offers to join Salsify are based on a few criteria, including the scope of the role, the candidate’s work experience, targeted skills, internal equity of the team, and external market data.

Salsify loves a good success story and it would be our privilege to help write yours! We recognize that talent and potential come in all forms and that years of experience does not guarantee on-the-job effectiveness or leadership potential.
